title: Evaporation-induced colloidal diffusiophoresis in electrolyte solutions
abstract: Non-volatile solutes accumulate near a receding drying front, generating concentration gradients that can drive directional colloidal transport by diffusiophoresis. This dynamic spatial arrangement of colloidal particles could affect the microstructure and macroscopic properties of the dried film. Here, we combine experiments and theory to investigate polystyrene particles suspended in electrolyte solutions drying within a capillary tube. By varying the electrolyte composition and ambient relative humidity, we show that evaporation-induced ion gradients drive particles toward the liquid-gas interface and enhance interfacial accumulation, whereas slower drying at higher humidity weakens the gradient and particle migration. We use the heat balance integral method to predict the transient solute field for a receding interface and couple it to particle transport to capture the observed parti
reason: Combines theory and experiment on colloidal diffusiophoresis driven by evaporation-induced ion gradients in a capillary.

title: Electro-Magnetohydrodynamic Flow of Nanofluids in Porous Microchannels: Modeling Dual Streaming Potentials with Dissipative and Joule Heating Effects
reason: Models streaming potentials and Joule heating in porous microchannels, covering coupled electrokinetic and thermal transport.

title: Using Salinity Gradients as an Energy Source to Produce Hydrogen
venue: Journal of Geoscience and Eco Agricultural Studies
abstract: Only renewable energy sources should be used to produce "green" hydrogen. Salinity gradient energy, which can be obtained by reversibly mixing solutions, offers several advantages over other renewable energy sources. Salinity gradient energy sources have high potential and energy density, and are stable. Using natural solutions has minimal adverse environmental impact. Membrane methods for converting salinity gradient energy have received the most development. Pilot industrial plants using osmotic semipermeable membranes and ion-selective membranes have been created. However, the technical characteristics of currently produced membranes and their high cost make salinity gradient energy uncompetitive compared to other renewable energy sources. Direct conversion of salinity gradient energy into electrical energy is possible through reverse electrodialysis in an electrodialysis battery cons
reason: Discusses reverse electrodialysis and ion-selective membranes for energy harvesting from salinity gradients.

title: Diffusioosmosis of electrolyte solutions in axisymmetric channels
abstract: We present a theory of fluid flow in long axisymmetric channels induced by salt concentration and pressure drops between their ends. The consideration is restricted to electrostatic diffuse layers that are thin compared to the local radius, but remains valid even when the concentration drop is quite large. We show that the magnitude of the diffusio-osmotic fluid flow rate QDO in a cylinder is the same as in a slit with a thickness equal to the cylinder diameter, whereas channels with variable cross sections can either retard or enhance it, depending on their geometry. The application of a pressure drop Δp≠0 results in an extra contribution QP to the total fluid flow rate Q without affecting QDO. reason: Develops theory for diffusio-osmotic flow in variable geometry channels, directly relevant to coupled transport.

title: Field- and Confinement-Modulated Unconventional Electroosmotic Flow in Two-Dimensional Graphene Nanochannels
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
abstract: Precise control of water and ion transport in nanochannels is fundamental to the development of functional nanofluidic devices. Recent experimental advances have enabled the exploration of nanoscale transport phenomena through the construction of two-dimensional channels with atomically tunable widths. Here, we show that unconventional electroosmotic flow occurring without an electric double layer (EDL) in two-dimensional nanochannels can be modulated by both the applied electric field and the channel width. Significant electroosmotic flow is observed in narrow channels when a single ion permeates under an external field. Free energy calculations of ion permeation events reveal that the flux is induced by channel selectivity for chloride ions over sodium ions. The flux undergoes an unexpected significant decrease when the channel broadens to a width of about 16 Å. This transition is attr
reason: Reveals field- and confinement-modulated unconventional electroosmosis in graphene nanochannels without EDL, relevant to nanoscale transport control.

title: Electric-Field Effects on Selective Transport through Graphene Nanopores
abstract: Selective ion transport through atomically thin membranes is central to next-generation desalination and nanofluidic technologies, yet how electric-field orientation couples with pore-size-dependent confinement to regulate the permeability-selectivity trade-off remains unresolved. Here, equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations systematically resolve pressure-driven water and NaCl transport through chemically unfunctionalized, charge-neutral monolayer graphene nanopores with diameters ranging from 0.73 to 1.91 nm under no-field, parallel-field, and perpendicular-field conditions. Pore diameter establishes the baseline water permeability and steric accessibility, whereas field orientation becomes mechanistically important in intermediate pores (∼1.0-1.5 nm), where ion entry remains sensitive to hydration-shell deformation and reorganization of pore-entrance water. reason: MD simulations of electric-field effects on selective ion transport through graphene nanopores for desalination.

title: Breaking Pore Symmetry to Prolong DNA Residence in Solid-State Nanopores
abstract: Abstract Rapid DNA transport limits the temporal resolution of solid-state nanopore sensing. Here we show that breaking pore symmetry through geometric inclination produces exceptionally prolonged DNA residence without surface functionalization or external trapping. For 500-base-pair double-stranded (ds) DNA, 13 nm diameter SiNx pores in tilted membranes exhibit a distinct long-lived population with a mean dwell time of 11.1 seconds at 600 mV bias, exceeding previously reported dsDNA dwell times by at-least 4 orders of magnitude. Controlled pore tilting reproduces the population of prolonged events, whose prevalence and duration depend on ionic strength. reason: Geometric pore asymmetry dramatically increases DNA dwell time in solid-state nanopores, enhancing sensing resolution.

title: Probing the pH- and Voltage-Driven Intramolecular Folding Dynamics of the c -MycC52 Promoter i -Motif at the Single-Molecule Level
abstract: The human c-Myc proto-oncogene is a transcription factor that regulates protein expression and is controlled by GC-rich regulatory sequences capable of adopting non-canonical DNA secondary structures. Here, we use the α-hemolysin (α-HL) protein nanopore to probe pH- and voltage-dependent effects on the stability of the i-motif formed by the 52-nucleotide cytosine-rich c-Myc promoter (c-MycC52). Under acidic conditions, electrophoretically driven c-MycC52 i-motifs are transiently trapped within the α-HL vestibule, generating pH-dependent electrical current signatures that are volumetrically and kinetically distinct and resolvable at the single-molecule level. The larger molecular volume measured in the acidic pH range, compared with that of linearized DNA at neutral pH, is consistent with the formation of an i-motif. reason: Single-molecule nanopore study of voltage- and pH-driven DNA i-motif dynamics, directly relevant to nanopore sensing.

title: Advances in Nanoconfined Transport: Characteristics, Theoretical Models, Measurement Techniques and Applications
abstract: Nanoconfined fluids exhibit unique transport behaviors that deviate fundamentally from the predictions of macroscopic transport models based on no-slip boundary conditions. The lack of theoretical frameworks has limited the progress toward disruptive separation and reaction nanotechnologies. This review synthesizes recent advances in nanoconfined transport from four perspectives. First, we examine the transport of fluids ranging from small molecules to polymers under nanoconfinement, and summarize their microstructural features, anomalous diffusion, and flow enhancement, as well as their correlations with key factors such as wall wettability, channel dimensions, and external fields. Then, the density, viscosity, slip, and flow models are outlined to better describe nanoconfined transport phenomena. Furthermore, nano- to microscale experimental techniques for probing confined-fluid struct
reason: Comprehensive review of nanoconfined fluid transport, theoretical models, and applications, directly relevant to electrokinetic and diffusio-kinetic phenomena.

title: Collective Fluid Coupling in Ultrathin Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for High-Performance Electrokinetic Energy Harvesting
abstract: Nanofluidic membranes hold promise for hydroelectric energy harvesting, but their output power is often limited by high fluidic impedance. Here, we fabricate ultrathin covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with AA-stacked, regular nanopore arrays. These membranes exhibit high fluid permeability exceeding 107 L m-2 h-1 bar-1, and record electrokinetic outputs with a streaming current density of 4.7 kA m-2 bar-1 and a power density of 12.8 W m-2 bar-1 in 1 M KCl. The high performance arises from the combination of ultrathin nature and collective interpore transport. Theoretical simulations reveal that the reduced interpore distance induces strong collective hydrodynamic coupling, which straightens streamlines, mitigates near-wall velocity dissipation, lowers fluidic resistance, and enhances net spatial charge density. reason: Ultrathin COF membranes with collective hydrodynamic coupling achieve record electrokinetic power density and scalable energy harvesting.

title: Decoupling Ion Transport from Water Flow in Rigid Subnanometer Channels for Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Conventional ion separation membranes employed for osmotic energy harvesting rely on nano- or subnanoscale channels that inherently facilitate the transport of hydrated ions, a mechanism that couples ion transport with parasitic solvent flow and fundamentally limits on energy conversion performance. Here, we break this paradigm by constructing continuous NASICON-type Li1.5Al0.5Ge1.5(PO4)3 membranes featuring rigid naked-ion transport channels. At this subnanometer scale, the channels no longer accommodate hydrated ions but enforce complete dehydration, enabling a naked-ion conduction mechanism. reason: Demonstrates naked-ion transport in subnanometer channels for high-performance osmotic energy harvesting, directly addressing coupled ion-water transport.

title: Unified Framework for Osmotic Energy Conversion
abstract: Abstract Osmotic energy systems employ charged nanoporous membranes and nanochannels to convert salinity gradients into electrical power, offering a promising route to harvest one of Earth’s most abundant yet underexploited renewable resources—the oceans—and providing reliable, carbon-free electricity. However, to date, no known self-consistent theoretical model can accurately predict the electrical response of realistic charge-selective systems. Thus, empirical and phenomenological models are used to increase the performance while attributing the increase to incorrect mechanisms. This leads to a costly empirical trial-and-error optimization process, which typically yields only incremental improvements. Here, we provide the first self-consistent theoretical model, verified by non-approximated numerical simulations, that establishes a detailed framework for osmotic energy conversion in re
reason: Provides a self-consistent theoretical model for osmotic energy conversion, including reservoir effects and analytical transport expressions.

title: Stacking-Controlled Reactivity and Friction of Water in Atomic-Scale hBN Channels from First Principles
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
abstract: Abstract Understanding the behavior of water confined in atomic-scale channels is a cornerstone of nanoscience and nanofluidics. Unlike graphene, isostructural hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spontaneously acquires electric charges in liquid water due to hydroxide ion (OH–) adsorption. Yet, whether this reactivity persists under monolayer and bilayer confinement remains an open question. Here, we use first-principles modeling to uncover the role of stacking symmetry (AA vs AA’) between hBN walls─a factor that has so far received little attention in boron nitride systems─on the structural and dynamical properties of Å-scale water. We systematically probe neutral, alkaline, and acidic environments to elucidate how water self-ions (H3O+ and OH–) interact with hBN interfaces. reason: Simulates water structure, ion adsorption, and friction in atomic-scale hBN channels, directly addressing confined transport physics.

title: Reconfigurable Nanofluidic Synapses Based on Polyaniline Protonation-Deprotonation Chemistry for Potential Bio-Integrated Computing
abstract: Abstract Polyaniline (PANI) has been extensively studied for decades, yet its reversible protonation-deprotonation (PDP) chemistry has remained unexploited in nanofluidic neuromorphic computing. Here we show that a porous PANI membrane, prepared by simple spin-coating, functions as a volatile ionic synapse whose short-term plasticity is chemically reconfigurable. Acid and base treatments reversibly switch the same device between paired-pulse facilitation and paired-pulse depressionopposing forms of synaptic behaviorthereby achieving chemically reconfigurable plasticity. Taking the base-configured state as a model system, the device exhibits spike-frequency, spike-amplitude, spike-duration, and spike-number dependent plasticity, revealing rich temporal dynamics. reason: Presents reconfigurable nanofluidic synapses using PANI protonation chemistry for neuromorphic computing, relevant to bio-integrated devices.

title: Ultrafast Nonlinear Vibrational Spectroscopy of Aqueous Solutions at Surfaces and in Heterogeneous Environments
abstract: Abstract Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. reason: Review of ultrafast spectroscopy probing electric double-layer formation and ion hydration at interfaces and in nanoconfinement.

title: Probing Inner-Tip Access-Resistance Modulation by ssDNA in a Nanopipette Using a Single-Molecule Nanomanipulation System
abstract: The transport of flexible polyelectrolytes through nanoscale confinements is fundamental to polymer physics and biophysics, yet direct observation remains challenging. Using a nanopipette-based single-molecule nanomanipulation platform, we controllably translocate long single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) through a solid-state nanopore, enabling real-time tracking of chain dynamics with nanoscale precision. We discover that ssDNA generates a characteristic progressive current decrease with terminal oscillations─absent for rigid double-stranded DNA. Evidence indicates this signal arises from inner-tip access-resistance modulation by the ssDNA coil, with a linear relationship between current blockade and relative escape displacement. Systematic variation of voltage and nanopore geometry reveals electric-field-driven stretching of the ssDNA coil and extended interaction with the inner tip region. Th
reason: Single-molecule study of ssDNA translocation in nanopore, directly relevant to nanopore sensing.

title: Intrinsic limits of ion enrichment and selectivity in charged nanopores: Insights from bulk-validated classical density functional theory with experimentally calibrated ion diameters
venue: International Journal of Modern Physics B
abstract: Understanding ion enrichment and selectivity in charged nanopores is essential for nanopore-based separation, desalination and sensing technologies. Here, we employ classical density functional theory (cDFT) with experimentally calibrated effective ion diameters to investigate equilibrium ion distributions in charged cylindrical nanopores. The cDFT framework is first validated against molecular dynamics simulations for bulk primitive-model electrolytes over different ion-sized ratios, concentrations and temperatures. title: Stability of electrokinetic Couette states in the Poisson--Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes system
abstract: In this paper, we study a two-dimensional Poisson--Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes system in a periodic channel driven by wall motion and an imposed tangential electric field, with two ionic species that may have unequal diffusivities. At the electroneutral Couette state, a diffusivity-weighted ionic energy combines with the triangular structure of the linearized operator to yield exponential linear stability for fixed \((A,E_0)\) and all positive diffusivities. Small-data nonlinear exponential stability is then obtained on a complex interpolation space adapted to the graph domain of the generator by combining analytic-semigroup smoothing with quadratic estimates. title: Cascaded Nano-ring Dialyzer for Continuous Regenerative Peritoneal Dialysis
abstract: ABSTRACT End-stage kidney disease (ESKD) requires lifelong kidney replacement therapy, yet conventional hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis remain limited by intermittent treatment, restricted mobility, and repeated dialysate exchange. Here, we developed a continuous regenerative peritoneal dialysis platform based on a cascaded nano-ring-assisted nanoelectrokinetic dialyzer for portable artificial kidney applications. We first identified key geometric and electrokinetic parameters governing the removal performance of nano-ring meshes, including mesh dimension, nano-ring coating thickness, the number of cascaded nano-rings, and the relative orientation between fluid flow and the applied electric field. We then developed a single cascaded nano-ring dialyzer operating at 1.33 mL/min and scaled the treatment capacity to approximately 10 mL/min through parallel integration of multiple module
reason: Nanoelectrokinetic dialyzer demonstrates electrokinetic transport in nanostructures for continuous dialysis.

title: Electrostatic Control of Li+ Density and Transport Rate in Double-Gated van der Waals Devices
abstract: Ion transport in crystalline hosts is controlled by an applied potential that simultaneously sets ionic distribution and transport rate, restricting operation to a one-dimensional control space. Here we show that the transport rate of Li+ ions in double-gated van der Waals devices can be modulated while the system occupies fixed ionic-density states. We measure the ionic current along the van der Waals interfaces between hexagonal boron nitride and graphene or MoS2 while simultaneously monitoring the in-plane electronic response. The ionic current exhibits pronounced hysteresis, with plateaus marking discrete ionic-density states balanced by electronic charge, while an independently tunable electrochemical-potential drop controls the ionic transport rate. reason: Demonstrates 2D electrostatic control of Li+ density and transport in van der Waals nanochannels.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Ion Transport in Nanopores: Fitting Implicit-Water Radial Diffusion Profiles to Explicit-Water Molecular Dynamics
abstract: We develop a multiscale approach for incorporating molecular-scale transport information into computationally efficient models of ion transport through nanopores. A radially varying effective diffusion coefficient profile is fitted to radial conductivity profiles obtained from explicit-water molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The fitting is performed within the NP+LEMC framework, which combines the Nernst--Planck equation with Local Equilibrium Monte Carlo to account for ion correlations beyond mean-field approximation. We apply the approach to NaCl, CaCl$_2$, and their mixtures in a negatively charged silica nanopore. The resulting diffusion coefficient profiles reproduce the radial current distributions of the MD simulations, including the strong suppression of ionic mobility near the pore wall that cannot be captured by a spatially constant diffusion coefficient inside the pore. reason: Multiscale modeling of ion transport in nanopores, fitting diffusion profiles to MD, highly relevant.

title: Viscoelectric Effect Influences Electroosmotic Flow in Charge-Regulated Microchannels
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
abstract: In this work, we study the combined influence of pH-dependent surface charge regulation and the viscoelectric effect on electroosmotic flow (EOF) in a charged microchannel. A semi-analytical model is developed to examine how the bulk pH, electrolyte concentration, and surface dissociation characteristics affect the electric-double layer and their eventual impact on the underlying flow. Results of this endeavour show that increasing the bulk pH initially enhances the electroosmotic flow by increasing the surface potential. However, at higher pH, the stronger electric field near the wall leads to a considerable increase in viscosity, which in turn, reduces the flow rate. The effect becomes more pronounced at higher electrolyte concentrations, where the thinner electrical-double layer produces a stronger electric field near the wall. title: Enhanced ionic diffusion by intrinsic liquid–gas slippage
abstract: Transport phenomena at liquid–gas interfaces remain not fully understood, particularly due to creating reproducible surfaces to quantify intrinsic slip and enhanced mass transport. Here we measure ionic diffusion currents across a bubble liquid film bounded by solid–liquid–gas interfaces under controlled salt gradients and surfactant concentrations. Ionic surfactant adsorption significantly increases the diffusion current, which peaks at 10 Superscript negative 1 10 − 1 $10^{-1}$ mM and decreases at higher concentrations. We attribute this non-monotonic behaviour to two competing effects: increased surface charge density and reduced slip length induced by surfactant adsorption. We develop an analytical theory for diffusion currents with slip boundaries, enabling extraction of the effective surface charge density and intrinsic slip length as functions of surfactant concentration. reason: Measures ionic diffusion currents with slip at liquid-gas interfaces, develops theory for slip-enhanced electrokinetic transport.

title: The Translocation of Circular DNA with Variable Single/Double Strand Ratios through Solid-State Nanopores: Transition from Entropic Barriers to Crowding-Dominated Kinetics
abstract: Solid-state nanopores serve as powerful single-molecule analytical platforms for characterizing the physicochemical signatures of nucleic acids and proteins, yet prior work has focused almost exclusively on linear DNA, leaving circular DNA translocation poorly understood, particularly how alternating single-/double-stranded (ss/ds) segments modulate transport kinetics. Here, a series of circular DNAs with discrete ssDNA fractions (0%, 33%, 66%, and 100%) was constructed and systematically interrogated for their voltage-dependent translocation through solid-state nanopores. Under fixed bias, ionic current blockade increases linearly with ss content, whereas dwell time scales exponentially with ss proportion. reason: Studies circular DNA translocation kinetics in solid-state nanopores, revealing entropic vs crowding regimes for sequencing.

title: A semi-analytical study on diffusiophoresis of pH-responsive diffuse soft particles
abstract: This study focuses on analyzing the diffusiophoresis of a diffuse soft particle comprising a hydrophobic rigid core coated with an inhomogeneous polyelectrolyte layer (PEL). Inhomogeneity in the diffuse PEL is incorporated by assuming that the polymer segment density varies spatially, resulting in a smooth transition in the electrohydrodynamic properties from the PEL to the bulk electrolyte. The PEL is further considered to contain zwitterionic functional groups, generating a pH-responsive volume charge density. A linear-perturbation technique is employed under the assumption of a weak concentration gradient, and the resulting coupled perturbed equations are solved using a finite-difference-based numerical method to determine the diffusiophoretic mobility. reason: Semi-analytical model of diffusiophoresis for pH-responsive soft particles, revealing chemiphoresis-electrophoresis coupling effects.

title: Functional Mimicry of Neural Sensory Systems Using Nanoporous Graphene-Based Ionic Biomimetic Tactile Devices
abstract: Tactile perception is essential for human interaction with the external world and holds significant potential in robotics, wearable devices, prosthetics, and healthcare. Conventional biomimetic tactile devices, which rely on electronic motion to generate electrical signals, deviate from the ionic transport mechanisms of biological systems, limiting their compatibility with biological tissues. This work proposed a biomimetic tactile device based on ionic transport mechanisms, leveraging electrokinetic energy conversion (EKEC) technology to generate electrical signals under pressure via an ion-selective membrane. The device was fabricated by modifying nanoporous graphene suspended on a porous polycarbonate track-etched polymer, followed by encapsulation in an ionic solution. reason: Demonstrates electrokinetic energy conversion via nanoporous graphene ion-selective membrane under pressure for biomimetic tactile sensing.

title: Non-Markovian Dynamics of Surface–Liquid Slip
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
abstract: Surface-liquid slip is critical in nanofluidic and confined biological systems, where interfacial effects dominate. Slip is typically described by a Markovian Navier friction coefficient, which fails to capture nonstationary friction dynamics. Here, a recent generalization of the Navier friction coefficient for subnanometer length scales is extended to describe the time evolution of surface-liquid friction down to subpicosecond time scales by a Navier memory kernel. Such kernels are extracted from combined equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of water adsorbed on chemically varied self-assembled monolayers (polar and nonpolar, fluorinated and nonfluorinated) and analyzed in the time and frequency domains. The Navier kernels exhibit spectral features associated with surface vibrational modes, revealing coupling between interfacial friction and substrate dynamics.
reason: Molecular dynamics reveals non-Markovian slip dynamics at solid-liquid interfaces, crucial for nanofluidic electrokinetic transport.

title: Molecular Dynamics of Ion Transport through Nanopores with Different Diameters for Applications in Nanofluidic Sensing
abstract: Abstract Nanopores have wide applications in nanofluidic sensing, energy conversion, and material separation, and their performance is closely related to ion transport through nanopores. In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are performed to systematically investigate dynamic ionic behaviors inside nanopores of varying diameters (D) from 2 to 10 nm under applied voltages. From radial ion distributions, the increase of D can modulate the ion concentration inside electric double layers (EDLs), especially for D changing from 2 to 5 nm. With ion numbers inside nanopores, the electroneutrality breakdown presents a linear decrease with D. reason: MD simulations reveal diameter-dependent ion transport, conductance scaling, and current noise in nanopores for nanofluidic sensing.

title: Effect of Electrolyte, Applied Voltage, and DNA Concentration on the Translocation Dynamics of a Single-Stranded DNA through a Solid-State Nanopore
abstract: Abstract Solid-state nanopores enable label-free detection of biomolecules by monitoring ionic current modulations during molecular translocation. However, reliable measurements are often limited by rapid, poorly controlled translocation dynamics producing short, low-resolution signals. Applied voltage, buffer composition, and analyte concentration influence molecular transport, yet their combined effect in ionic environments, including Tris-based buffers, remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated the effects of applied voltage, DNA concentration, and buffer composition on translocation kinetics of a circular 7560-nucleotide single-stranded DNA and the current blockage characteristics. reason: Studies DNA translocation dynamics in solid-state nanopores under varying voltage, buffer, concentration; relevant to nanopore sensing.

title: Confinement‐Induced Donnan Potential Enables Sealed Hydrovoltaic Power From Microliter Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrovoltaic power generation offers a promising route for sustainable energy generation, yet existing systems typically rely on evaporation‐driven flow or environmental moisture gradients, limiting device encapsulation and compact integration. Here, we introduce a confinement‐induced ion‐selective mechanism that enables sealed hydrovoltaic power generation from minimal water input. By engineering asymmetric nanochannel confinement in MXene/cellulose nanofiber (CNF) composites, localized hydration generates spatially distinct cation selectivity, establishing a persistent ion gradient and a confinement‐dependent Donnan potential that drives capacitive charge accumulation. The harvested energy derives from substantial interfacial free energy released upon hydration of nanochannels with a high surface‐to‐volume ratio. reason: Demonstrates sealed hydrovoltaic power generation via confinement-induced Donnan potential in nanochannels, directly relevant to energy harvesting and electrokinetic energy conversion.

title: Electroosmotic Flow Enhancement in Subnanometer Carbon Nanotubes Triggered by Water Ordering Cooperatively Induced by an Electric Field and Ion
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
abstract: Abstract Ion and water transport through subnanometer carbon nanotubes (CNTs) exhibits numerous anomalies absent in bulk solutions, yet the interplay among the confined water structure, external electric fields, and ion transport remains poorly understood. Here, we use systematic nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to study single-file water confined in a CNT of radius 0.37 nm, both in the absence and presence of a single Na+ ion, under applied electric fields ranging from 0 to 0.2 V Å–1. In the Na+–water–CNT system, the electroosmotic flow (EOF) velocity increases nonlinearly with the field. Such nonlinear enhancement is attributed to water ordering that is exclusive to the ion-containing system. reason: Reveals electroosmotic flow enhancement in subnanometer CNTs via ion-induced water ordering, uncovering nanoscale electrokinetic coupling.

title: Theory of magneto-electrokinetics in unidirectional electrolyte flow: hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect
abstract: We develop a theoretical framework for magneto-electrokinetic transport in dilute electrolytes under unidirectional flow and streaming current conditions. Unlike standard magnetohydrodynamics in liquid metals, where charge carriers are electrons and conductivity is typically uniform, electrolytes exhibit spatially varying ion densities and additional forces such as osmotic pressure. In steady state, the coupled Navier–Stokes, Nernst–Planck and Poisson equations become analytically tractable. We derive a Boltzmann-like expression for ion distributions that incorporates both the electrostatic potential and a novel hydrodynamic potential arising from the magnetic field. This potential depends explicitly on the flow profile and is not screened close to the bounding walls. reason: Theoretical framework for magneto-electrokinetic transport deriving hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect in electrolyte flow.

title: In-Plane Heterostructures Enable Deterministic and Repeated Biomolecular Sensing by Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
abstract: Abstract Applications of plasmonic nanopores for molecular sequencing remain limited by poorly controlled translocation dynamics and predominantly single-pass readout. Here, we propose an in-plane heterostructure architecture that integrates molecular transport, confinement, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) readout to enable deterministic and repeated interrogation of individual biomolecules. Using all-atom molecular dynamics coupled with nanoplasmonic simulations, we show that the heterostructure can actively guide molecules into and through a localized sensing region while constraining their conformational and translational dynamics. Simulated SERS signatures discriminate single-stranded DNA sequences with resolution approaching the single-nucleobase scale and further suggest the feasibility of distinguishing polyglutamine tracts of different lengths. Importantly, the in-pl
reason: Proposes in-plane heterostructure for controlled, repeated nanopore sensing of biomolecules, advancing DNA sequencing.

title: Preferential Transport of Mg2+ over Li+ in Negatively Charged Styrene Sulfonate-Regulated Graphene Oxide Nanochannels
abstract: Abstract Efficient lithium recovery from salt-lake brines is severely hindered by their high Mg2+/Li+ ratios. Recent nanofiltration technologies primarily directly extract lithium from brine, which incurs high energy consumption. Herein, using pressure-driven molecular dynamics simulations at 5 MPa (representative of practical operating pressures), we propose a strategy for preferential Mg2+ transport over Li+ to lower the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratios for further low-energy lithium extraction, based on intercalating styrene sulfonate inside graphene oxide nanochannels (SS–@GO). The results demonstrate a reversal in permeation selectivity from Li+ to Mg2+ upon negatively charging the lamellar channel through SS– insertion at an interlayer spacing of 1.8 nm (d). reason: MD simulation shows selective Mg2+ over Li+ transport in charged graphene oxide nanochannels for brine pretreatment.

title: Recovering Rare Earth Elements from Mining Effluent via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated Coordination in MXene Membranes
abstract: Abstract Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand–metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M
reason: Demonstrates selective REE recovery via angstrom-scale confinement and coordination in MXene nanochannels.

title: When Heating Enhances Dielectric Screening: Thermal Disordering of Surface-Templated Antiferroelectric Order Reverses the Temperature Response of Interfacial Water
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
abstract: Abstract The in-plane dielectric constant (ε∥) of nanoconfined water plays an essential role in temperature-gated nanofluidics and reaction kinetics at electrochemical interfaces. Water monolayers with antiferroelectric rhombic order on fcc(100) surfaces have been shown, in our previous work, to exhibit an anomalously low ε∥, but how this dielectric response evolves with temperature is unexplored. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we find that ε∥ of water on the fcc(100) surface increases monotonically with temperature, in stark contrast to the monotonic decrease observed on fcc(111) surfaces and in bulk water. This anomaly originates from the progressive thermal disordering of the antiferroelectric rhombic structure, releasing previously suppressed dipolar fluctuations. Consequently, the enhancement of the Kirkwood factor GK overcomes both the conventional 1/T thermal suppression an
reason: Thermal disordering of interfacial water alters dielectric response for nanofluidics.

title: Water-Transport Resistance of Perfluorosulfonic-Acid (PFSA) Membranes: Delineating the Role of Interface and Chemistry
abstract: Abstract The proton-exchange membrane (PEM) is an integral component in PEM fuel cells, water electrolyzers, and other electrochemical energy-conversion devices. In these devices, the PEM must conduct protons but inhibit reactant/product gas crossover; its operation depends heavily on its hydration level. Furthermore, PEMs exhibit complicated water management balanced between transport phenomena, interfacial resistance, and the electro-osmosis vs back-transport trade-off, all of which also depend on external environmental conditions. In this paper, we investigate interfacial and bulk water-transport resistance for perfluorosulfonic-acid (PFSA) membranes with long, medium, and short side-chain lengths (Nafion, 3M, and Aquivion, respectively) in controlled temperature-humidity environments. Using a factorial design of experiments based on 12 chemistry-thickness × 16 environmental condition
reason: Quantifies water transport resistance and electro-osmosis in PFSA membranes for PEM fuel cells/electrolyzers, key for energy harvesting membranes.

title: Confined gases enable coupled heat–mass transport in nanoporous materials
abstract: Heat conduction in gas-loaded nanoporous materials is generally interpreted as phonon transport through the host framework, with adsorbed molecules treated primarily as passive phonon scattering centers. Here we demonstrate that this picture becomes incomplete under nanoconfinement, where mobile adsorbates actively participate in heat transport through coupled heat–mass transport. Combining equilibrium molecular dynamics with linear irreversible thermodynamics, we decompose the effective thermal conductivity into framework-mediated, guest-mediated, and Onsager cross-coupling contributions. For methane-loaded MOF-5 we show that the thermal conductivity increases with gas loading despite a reduction in molecular diffusivity. This seemingly counterintuitive behavior originates from the growth of guest-mediated enthalpy transport and correlations between heat and mass currents. Idealized nan
reason: Confined gases actively drive coupled heat-mass transport via Onsager cross-coupling in nanopores.

title: How to Engineer Biological Nanopores for Single-Molecule Capture and Discrimination
abstract: Abstract Protein-based biological nanopores have emerged as versatile tools for sequencing biopolymers, identifying molecules, and probing reactions at the single-molecule level. Many biological nanopores have been characterized, revealing the significance of nanopore size, shape, and chemical composition in molecular detection and discrimination. Advancements in understanding the nanofluidic properties of nanopores have complemented engineering approaches expanding the possible applications of nanopore technology. Through a combination of structural insights, rational design, systematic screening, and molecular dynamics simulations, researchers have developed nanopores capable of distinguishing between ions, nucleic acids, peptides, and folded proteins with remarkable specificity and sensitivity. Building upon three decades of progress, this Review highlights recent engineering innovati
reason: Review on engineering biological nanopores for single-molecule sensing, directly relevant to nanopore applications.

title: Boosted Energy Extraction from the CapMix Process by Grafting with Titratable Polymers
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
abstract: Abstract Salinity gradient energy offers a sustainable route to convert ionic chemical potential differences into usable power. Capacitive mixing enables this conversion without membranes, but suffers from limited ion regulation at electrode interfaces. Here we show that, by grafting electrode surfaces with titrating polymers, the performance can be substantially improved. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations with exact image-charge Ewald summations, we demonstrate how the coupled effects of ion adsorption and charge regulation in response to an external potential can be harnessed. Grafted electrodes are shown to deliver substantially more energy relative to bare surfaces, driven by charge regulation effects that exploit the pH difference that typically exists between rivers and the ocean. While the effect is in principle maximized at high grafting densities and moderate chain l
reason: Shows enhanced capacitive mixing energy harvesting via polymer grafting, relevant to salinity-gradient power.

title: Migration Mechanism Regulated by the Coupling between Ions and Charged Nanoparticles in Janus Nanochannels
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
abstract: Charged nanoparticle migration through asymmetric nanochannels is important for particle separation, nanoscale drug delivery, and nanofluidic regulation. However, in electrolyte solutions, particle transport is governed not only by the applied electric field or fixed channel charges but also by local ion distributions, particle counterion clouds, and electro-osmotic responses. Here, a Janus nanochannel model was constructed, and molecular dynamics simulations investigated the translocation of positively charged nanoparticles through an asymmetric fixed-charge channel. Increasing the positive charge at the right end increased particle residence time near the Janus interface and positively charged gating region, promoted counterion enrichment around the particle, and weakened local water flow assistance. reason: MD simulation of charged nanoparticle translocation in Janus nanochannels reveals ion-particle coupling effects on electrokinetic transport.

title: Field-induced interfacial charge organisation in strongly confined graphene and silicene nanochannels: a molecular dynamics study
abstract: Electric double layer (EDL) formation governs ion transport in nanoconfined systems, yet the coupled roles of ionic properties, solvent organisation and confinement remain incompletely understood. Classical molecular dynamics simulations are used to analyse field-induced interfacial charge organisation in realised graphene and silicene nanochannels containing mono-, di- and trivalent ions. Time-resolved migration, steady-state confinement statistics, ion and water number-density distributions, and solvent-forcing simulations are evaluated. Both systems develop persistent interfacial ionic organisation, but localisation and positional fluctuations remain strongly ion-specific rather than following a simple valence trend. Graphene frequently produces sharper ion-density maxima and more strongly structured water distributions, whereas silicene generally supports broader profiles across its
reason: MD reveals ion-specific interfacial organization in graphene/silicene nanochannels under electric fields.

title: Interfacial Adsorption–Desorption of Ionic Surfactants and Charge-Density Inversion in Droplet Electrophoresis with Multivalent Electrolytes
abstract: Abstract The electrophoresis of a viscous droplet coated with sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), an anionic surfactant, in a nonamphiphilic electrolyte containing valence-asymmetric salts is investigated. The lateral mobility and kinetic exchange of surfactant molecules at the droplet interface lead to a nonuniform surfactant distribution, generating Marangoni stresses and enhancing electric double-layer (EDL) polarization. Consequently, the electrophoretic response of the droplet differs from predictions based on the conventional assumption of a constant and immobile surface charge density. To account for these effects, we develop a modified electrokinetic model incorporating finite-sized and electrostatically correlated ions. reason: Develops electrokinetic model for droplet electrophoresis with surfactant dynamics and ion correlations, relevant to fundamental electrokinetic transport.

title: Wood‐MOF Thermoelectrics for Heat and Power Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoelectric materials and devices enable to harvest heat energy from the environment, which offers a promising solution for addressing the critical issue of conventional fossil fuels for energy supply. However, sustainable development of low‐grade heat conversion to electricity is limited by materials and technologies. Herein, inspired by the conduction of water molecules and ions in trees, natural wood is chemically modified and synthesized to a nanostructured wood/metal‐organic framework (wood/MOF) gradient, in which it enables the driving of the ions movements through charged nanochannels for enhancing the generation of the thermally generated voltage. This has resulted in a 1200% increased differential thermal voltage of wood/MOF gradient compared to that of natural wood due to the thermophoretic mobility difference between the negative and positive ions. reason: Wood/MOF gradient harvests heat via ion thermophoresis in charged nanochannels, direct relevance.

title: Structure-Guided Conversion of a TonB-Dependent Transporter into a Functional β-Barrel Nanopore
abstract: Abstract Protein nanopores are valuable platforms for single-molecule sensing; however, expanding the range of structurally defined nanopores remains challenging. We describe a minimal, structure-guided redesign strategy that converts BtuB, a TonB-dependent vitamin B12 transporter, into a functional β-barrel nanopore. Using protein structure prediction and molecular dynamics, we eliminated the internal plug domain, selected extracellular loops, and preserved the 22-stranded β-barrel scaffold. BtuBΔ1–136_Δloops formed single channels in planar lipid bilayers, exhibiting an approximately linear current–voltage relationship and a single-channel conductance of ∼1.2 nS. Polymer exclusion analysis revealed an apparent PEG-accessible diameter of approximately 4 nm, indicating a highly accessible pore entrance. Noise analysis showed that extracellular loop architecture influences the stability o
reason: Engineers a β-barrel nanopore and characterizes its ion transport properties, directly relevant to nanopore transport physics.

title: Crossover from Asymmetric to Symmetric Electrowetting Linked to Double-Layer Restructuring
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Voltage-controlled wetting at solid-liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry
reason: Atomistic simulation and experiment reveal double-layer restructuring causes electrowetting asymmetry, fundamental to electrokinetic interfacial phenomena.

title: Nonlinear electrophoresis of a dielectric particle in a non-polar media. Part I. Intermediate Debye numbers
abstract: The electrophoresis of a charged dielectric particle in a low conductivity non-polar media is numerically investigated over a wide range of parameters. Association/dissociation reactions that may alter the concentration of free charge carriers in weak non-polar media are not included in the present model. The results are compared with previously published experimental data, revealing a universal relaxation behaviour of the ionic cloud. We describe an electrophoretic regime observed at intermediate Debye numbers and relatively high Dukhin numbers. In this regime, non-equilibrium effects become important and the Smoluchowski formula is no longer applicable. Two charged layers with high tangential fluxes of counterions and coions are identified. reason: Fundamental numerical study of nonlinear electrophoresis in non-polar media, revealing non-equilibrium double-layer physics.

title: Shear-induced electrophoretic migration perpendicular to the electric field
abstract: Recent experiments have shown that microparticles subjected simultaneously to electrophoresis and pressure-driven flow undergo lateral migration. Although fluid inertia has been proposed to explain this phenomenon, it remains negligible in these regimes, leaving the underlying mechanism an open question. In this work, we demonstrate that concentration polarisation alone can account for this effect. By modelling a dielectric particle with finite surface conductance in a shear flow, we show that the flow breaks the symmetry of the ionic cloud in the direction perpendicular to the applied electric field. title: Merging molecular dynamics with homogenisation: a novel strategy for the modelling of nano-filtration phenomena
abstract: Filtration flows through nanoporous membranes play a crucial role in a range of cutting-edge technologies, including water purification, osmotic power generation and targeted drug delivery. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are currently considered the state-of-the-art approach for modelling nano-filtration processes. However, their high computational cost makes simulating large-scale filtration systems impractical, limiting the ability to conduct extensive parametric studies and optimise design strategies. In the present paper, we merge a molecular analysis of the nano-filtration problem with a homogenisation technique, to upscale the filtration flow from the single nanopore description to the whole membrane scale phenomenon. reason: Multiscale modeling of nanoporous membrane filtration for water purification and osmotic power generation.

title: Electroosmotic Flow Modulation and Dispersion of Uncharged Solutes through a Reservoir-Connected Soft Nanochannel
abstract: Abstract The present study investigates the modulation of the electroosmotic flow (EOF) and the transport and dispersion of uncharged solutes in a reservoir-connected soft nanochannel containing different electrolytes. The nanochannel walls are charged and coated with a fluid- and ion-permeable polyelectrolyte layer (PEL) with a distributed volumetric charge density, while the reservoir walls are uncoated and electrically neutral. The electrokinetic model is formulated within the continuum framework by incorporating ion–ion electrostatic correlations, steric effects, ion–solvent interactions, concentration-dependent viscosity, and the resulting spatial variation in ionic diffusivity. A modified electrostatic body force is included in the momentum equation to capture the coupled electrohydrodynamic behavior. reason: Studies EOF modulation and solute dispersion in reservoir-connected soft nanochannels with polyelectrolyte layers, showing flow reversal.

title: Confined Water Wires as Anisotropic Proton Highways in a Neutral Polymer Single Crystal
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Directional proton transport is central to bioenergetics and emerging electrochemical technologies, yet achieving high and anisotropic proton conductivity in fully covalent, charge-neutral crystalline materials remains a challenge. Here, we report anisotropic proton conduction in a one-dimensional covalent polymer single crystal mediated by confined water wires. A phenylalanine-tyrosine-based monomer bearing azide and alkyne termini undergoes topochemical click reaction via large-amplitude molecular rotations, yielding a 1,4-triazole-linked one-dimensional polymer through a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation. The polymerization concomitantly generates hydrophobic nanochannels that reversibly capture atmospheric water, within which water molecules self-assemble into extended hydrogen-bonded chains. reason: Shows anisotropic proton conduction via confined water wires in neutral polymer nanochannels, relevant to ion transport in nanoconfinement.

title: Multiplexed Small-Molecule Detection Using Sequence-Defined DNA Reporters in an Argonaute−Nanopore System
abstract: Abstract Multiplexed small-molecule detection remains challenging because chemically diverse analytes lack universal amplification and encoding mechanisms. Here, we present SMART-pore, a programmable molecular encoding-decoding platform, that converts target recognition events into sequence-defined DNA reporters and resolves them through machine-learning-assisted nanopore fingerprinting. A modular reporter architecture comprising a cobalamin (Cbl) anchor, an encoding domain, and an electrophoretic guiding segment was developed to generate orthogonal nanopore signatures. Target-induced release of guide DNAs activates PfAgo-mediated cleavage, producing sequence-defined DNA fragments that can be readily transformed into nanopore-readable reporters through a simple Cbl-capping reaction. Four representative mycotoxins (AFB1, OTA, PAT, and ZEN) were simultaneously detected with picomolar sensi
reason: Nanopore-based multiplexed small-molecule detection using DNA reporters, advancing nanopore sensing.

title: Effect of Confinement on Ion Transport in Polymer Electrolytes
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
abstract: Understanding ion transport in polymer electrolytes is important for elucidating the molecular origins of transport limitations and opportunities in nanostructured solid polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate how cylindrical confinement regulates the structure and dynamics of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based electrolytes. Decreasing the nanotube diameter drives pronounced polymer chain segregation and reorganizes the spatial distribution of coordinating oxygen sites. This confinement-induced structural rearrangement markedly suppresses ion-segment codiffusion along short chain segments and inhibits interchain hopping, leading to a substantial decrease in Li+ mobility. reason: Molecular dynamics reveals confinement effects on ion transport in polymer electrolytes inside nanotubes, directly relevant to nanochannel transport.

title: Influence of yield stress on electroosmotic flow mixing in a charged modulated microchannel
abstract: This study numerically investigates vortex-induced electroosmotic mixing of a Casson viscoplastic fluid in a wavy microchannel with sinusoidally heterogeneous surface charge. The coupled electrokinetic transport is described using the Navier–-Stokes–Poisson–Nernst–Planck formulation, while the flow, stress, and species-concentration fields are resolved using a finite volume method. The analysis reveals a coupled mechanism in which wall corrugation and spatially varying surface charge generate transverse recirculation and enlarge the interfacial contact area between the incoming streams, whereas the yield stress modifies the flow through the formation and growth of unyielded regions. Increasing the wave amplitude α and yield-stress parameter τ0 enhances mixing, although the latter simultaneously increases flow resistance and pressure loss. reason: Numerically investigates electroosmotic mixing of yield-stress fluid in charge-modulated microchannel, core electrokinetic transport.

title: Electroosmotic Dispersion in Convergent-Divergent Flow Pathways: The Role of Rheology-Dependent Analyte Diffusion
abstract: This study investigates rheology-dependent analyte transport under electroosmotic flow in a converging-diverging narrow fluidic channel. The analysis employs the Carreau constitutive model to describe the fluid rheology, while the Stokes-Einstein relation is used to account for viscosity-dependent molecular diffusion. The coupled electrokinetic and species transport equations are solved numerically. The correlative effects of flow configuration geometry, fluid rheology, and electrokinetic parameters on the analyte diffusion and its eventual impact on transient dispersion are systematically examined. The results reveal that shear-thinning rheology produces significant spatial variations in apparent viscosity, leading to nonuniform diffusion coefficients throughout the channel. reason: Fundamental study of electroosmotic dispersion in microchannels with shear-thinning rheology and geometry effects.

title: Modeling and simulation of the electrohydrodynamics for dielectric to high-conductivity liquids
abstract: Electrohydrodynamics investigates the fluid motion driven by electric fields. It provides the theoretical foundation for applications such as high-resolution printing and electrospray. However, existing electrohydrodynamic (EHD) models often suffer from unreal charge diffusion across the mixed fluid–fluid interface. This unreal charge leakage can severely affect numerical convergence and solution accuracy, particularly in systems with extremely large conductivity contrasts between the two phases, where the conductivity ratio exceeds 1013. In this study, a new two-phase EHD model is developed to calculate the EHD phenomena, coupling the flow field, electric field, and phase field. A novel transition function framework is proposed to ensure the smooth and rapid change of electric parameters across the interface, thereby suppressing the unreal charge diffusion. reason: Presents a two-phase EHD model with Poisson-Nernst-Planck charge transport, advancing fundamental electrokinetic simulation.

title: Electrophoresis of a polymeric Brinkman droplet in a cylindrical pore
abstract: Electrophoresis of a nondeforming polymeric Brinkman droplet with a constant surface potential in an uncharged cylindrical pore is investigated theoretically. The droplet is modeled as a polymer-containing fluid inclusion whose internal flow is resisted by a Debye–Büeche–Brinkman (DBB) hydrodynamic drag. An analytical relation converting the polymer-induced internal drag into an equivalent Newtonian viscosity is derived. A patched pseudo-spectral method based on Chebyshev polynomials is adopted to solve the coupled electrostatic, ionic-transport, and hydrodynamic equations. The results show that the boundary confinement effect is most profound in narrow pores. In addition to the extra hydrodynamic resistance, the nearby wall squeezes and deforms the electric double layer, thereby enhancing the motion-deterring double-layer polarization. reason: Theoretical analysis of electrophoresis of a polymeric droplet in a cylindrical pore, revealing confinement and double-layer polarization effects.

title: Electrohydrodynamic migration of charged non-spherical particles in non-Newtonian Poiseuille flows
abstract: The precise active manipulation of complex suspensions plays a critical role in frontier applications such as microfluidic cell sorting, electrochemical crystallization, and polymer composite processing. Therefore, this study develops a mesoscopic computational framework based on the diffuse-interface lattice Boltzmann method to investigate the electrohydrodynamic migration of charged highly anisotropic particles in non-Newtonian Poiseuille flows. By coupling the leaky dielectric model with generalized power-law constitutive equations, the dynamic interplay among background shear-flow, localized rheological modifications, and external electrostatic driving forces is decoupled. reason: Simulates electrohydrodynamic migration of anisotropic particles in non-Newtonian microchannel flows.

title: Electrolyte density, diffusivity and conductivity in graphene nanoconfinement predicted by separating interfacial from genuine confinement effects
abstract: Confined aqueous electrolytes exhibit strong deviations from bulk behaviour, but it remains unclear which changes arise from genuine confinement-induced modification and which merely reflect the influence of interfaces. Here, we introduce an interfacial deficit-length framework, capable of decomposing density, diffusivity, and conductivity of confined electrolyte solutions into interfacial and confinement contributions. By applying the framework to molecular dynamics simulations of aqueous alkali halides in planar graphene nanoslits coupled to bulk reservoirs at variable electrolyte concentration, we show that genuine confinement effects emerge only for slit heights $H \lesssim 1$ nm; for larger H, deviations from bulk behaviour are quantitatively captured by interfacial deficit lengths. These deficit lengths are strongly ion-specific and generally positive for water and salt densities a
reason: Decomposes confinement vs interfacial effects on electrolyte properties in graphene nanoslits, directly relevant to nanochannel ion transport.

title: Beyond the Ohmic Limit: Co-Ion Control and Conductance Scaling Regimes in Rectifying Nanochannels
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
abstract: The power-law scaling of ionic conductance G ∼ cα serves as a fundamental probe of transport physics in confined geometries, where transport is traditionally restricted to sublinear regimes (α 1) in bipolar configurations while driving unipolar ones toward linearity (α ∼ 1). By unifying biological and solid-state membranes under a single predictive model, these findings clarify how pore geometry, charge asymmetry, and voltage polarity cooperatively govern nanoscale ion transport.
reason: Explores conductance scaling and co-ion control in rectifying nanochannels, directly addressing fundamental ion transport physics in confined geometries.

title: MXene-Coated Hair Fibers as a Versatile Platform for Flexible Electronics, Intelligent Sensing, and Energy Harvesting
abstract: Abstract Hair fibers with α-keratin biopolymers are responsive to water owing to the reversible disruption and formation of hydrogen bonds, which can be constructed as a hygrometer. However, the functionality is insufficient in smart sensors and energy harvesting because of their intrinsic insulation. Herein, electrically conductive hair fibers are produced by the layer-by-layer assembly method through forming MXene sheaths. Bovine serum albumin (BSA) with a positive charge is assembled firstly onto the hair fibers, and MXene nanosheets are adsorbed on the surface of the hair through electrostatic interactions. Due to the superior electrical conductivity of MXene and water responsivity of hair, hair fibers can be used in electric devices with enhanced mechanical properties and humidity sensitivity. title: Molecular Programming of Steric Tags for Controlled Nanopore Translocation toward Precision Clinical Diagnostic Assistance
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The precise resolution of single-molecule events is often limited by the stochastic thermal motion of analytes, which traverse nanoscale sensing zones too rapidly for conventional detection bandwidths. This remains a fundamental challenge in nanopore chemistry, particularly for small and flexible peptides. Here, we report a chemically intuitive molecular programming strategy─steric blockage-enabled slow translocation (SLOW-Trans)─that overcomes this physical limitation through the rational design of sterically demanding probe molecules. By site-specifically conjugating rigid aromatic steric tags with precisely defined dimensions to peptide substrates, we actively reshape the translocation energy landscape within the ∼1.2 nm constriction of the M2MspA nanopore. reason: Programs steric tags to control peptide translocation in MspA nanopore for clinical diagnostics, advancing nanopore sensing.

title: Improving All-Atom Molecular Dynamics Models for Quantitative Prediction of Nanopore Blockade Current
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
abstract: All-atom molecular dynamics has become an indispensable tool in development of nanopore sensors of biological information. In a typical nanopore experiment, measurements of ionic current flowing through a nanopore report on the chemical structure of biomolecules that pass through the nanopore. Such experiments alone are often insufficient to relate the structure of the biomolecules to the ionic current modulations. The molecular dynamics method can establish such a relationship directly through a brute force simulation under applied electric field. Here, we examine the ability of molecular dynamics force fields to reproduce experimentally measured nanopore blockade currents produced by single-stranded DNA. Our simulations show that none of the "off the shelf" force fields (CHARMM36, AMBER Parmbsc1 and DES-AMBER) is capable of reproducing experimental data with the desired level of accura
reason: Refines MD force fields to accurately simulate nanopore blockade currents, advancing computational electrokinetics.

title: Diffusion of charged rods across 3D varying section channels
abstract: We analyze the transport of rod-like particles by diffusion and drift in a three-dimensional channel with varying circular or elliptic cross section. Applying the Fick-Jacobs approximation to the transport equation of the particles' probability distribution, we derive an effective one-dimensional substitute model and the associated free energy profile. Our results show that the data for the mean first passage time of rods, once expressed as a function of the effective free energy barrier, collapse onto the same master curve as obtained for point or spherical particles. The observed universality provides a simple framework for predicting transport times of anisotropic particles in confined geometries without resolving the full multidimensional dynamics.
reason: Theoretical model for diffusion and drift of charged rods in varying cross-section channels, relevant to electrokinetic transport in confined geometries.

title: A geometry optimization framework for enhancement of ionic current rectification
abstract: Ionic current rectification (ICR) is central to nanofluidics and iontronics, yet current nanopore designs often rely on parametric scans of predefined geometries, which limits their performance. This work presents a geometry optimization framework to inversely design charged nanoslits for the maximization of ICR. Treating the electrolyte-electrode interface as a continuous design variable governed by the steady-state Poisson-Nernst-Planck system, a shape gradient flow algorithm is developed to optimize the geometry. Within this framework, shape calculus is employed to perform sensitivity analysis, deriving expressions supported on the moving boundary. Without relying on predefined templates, optimization achieves higher rectification ratios than standard linear conical nanoslits. Thorough investigation reveals that the algorithm autonomously generates highly asymmetric geometries. Three
reason: Presents a geometry optimization framework for ionic current rectification in nanoslits using shape calculus and PNP model.

title: Decoupled capacitive-gate electro-osmosis: Phase-controlled bidirectional flow in high-conductivity electrolytes via a modified Poisson–Boltzmann–Stokes framework
abstract: Alternating-current electro-osmosis in high-conductivity electrolytes (σ ≈ 1.68 S m−1) is constrained by a single Resistance Capacitance (RC)-pole operating window: Flow velocity peaks at the electric double layer charging frequency fRC and collapses steeply on either side, while attempts to widen the band by raising electrode voltage drive Faradaic reactions that are incompatible with physiological media. We present a decoupled electrokinetic architecture in which a buried capacitive gate electrode independently modulates the wall zeta potential through a thin Al2O3 dielectric, while asymmetric propulsion electrodes generate the tangential field in the bulk.
