reason: Presents decoupled capacitive-gate electro-osmosis for bidirectional flow in high-conductivity electrolytes, novel electrokinetic architecture.

title: Modified Ewald Summation Method for Slab Geometries: Application to Donnan Potentials, Confinement Electrostatics, and Titration Simulations
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
abstract: Simulating electrochemical systems confined within nanoscale slab geometries is a major challenge due to long-range electrostatic interactions and the breakdown of global charge neutrality when the domain exchanges ions with an external bulk electrolyte reservoir. In this work, we present a grand-canonical simulation framework designed for slab geometries that utilizes a regularized 3D periodic Ewald summation technique to systematically converge to the true 2D periodic Green's function without unphysical cell-width (Lz) dependencies. Unlike traditional grand canonical methods that rely on neutral-pair insertions to maintain a zero net charge, our framework allows the net cell charge to fluctuate by implementing decoupled, single-ion trial moves. This approach bypasses the cooperative sampling bottlenecks that plague neutral-pair insertions inside dense, strongly charged nanopores. Cruci
reason: Grand-canonical simulation framework for slab geometries enabling Donnan potential calculation in nanoscale electrochemical systems.

title: Probing Acetylcholinesterase Activity and Enzyme Inhibitor Evaluation by Electrostatic-Gating Nanopores
abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) plays a crucial role in neuron function and is closely associated with neurodegenerative diseases. Probing AChE-mediated catalytic reactions in biomimetic scenarios (e.g., micro- and nanospace) is of fundamental significance. Here, we present an artificial nanopore to investigate AChE activity by catalyzing acetylcholine (ACh) hydrolysis. In this assay, a predesigned glass nanopore facilitated the electrostatic assembly of the substrate, ACh. Under optimized conditions, AChE exhibited a high catalytic efficiency of up to 94% in a confined environment. The surface charge alteration due to the catalytic reaction was able to regulate ion-gating behavior and ionic current rectification (ICR). In addition, the Michaelis-Menten constant (Km) was calculated to be 26.45 mM, indicating the enhanced catalytic efficiency in the confinement, as compared to that of a conve
reason: Uses electrostatic-gating nanopore to probe enzyme kinetics and inhibitor screening, demonstrating confined electrokinetic sensing.

title: AI-assisted analytical theory in soft matter and multiphysics: new results and lessons from diffusiophoresis and bipolar membranes
abstract: We present a framework to advance analytical theory in the area of soft matter and multiphysics using assistance from AI. The framework emphasizes (i) setting "honesty rules", (ii) focusing on a few key papers that are used to formulate a problem of interest, (iii) specifying checks a priori, (iv) using only one task per session and keeping a running log of tasks, checks, corrections, and sessions so that a mistake is not propagated through a project, and (v) ensuring all decisions are approved by humans while AI focuses primarily on execution. The framework is applied to two distinct problems to create new knowledge, including (i) diffusiophoresis of a spherical particle in the presence of an arbitrary number of electrolytes at arbitrary Debye lengths, and (ii) analytical description of I-V curves, including overlimiting current, in bipolar membranes without including the water dissocia
reason: Develops AI-assisted analytical theory for diffusiophoresis and bipolar membranes, directly relevant to diffusio-kinetic transport and electrodialysis.

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Two-Dimensional Molybdenum Oxide Nanostructures for High-Performance Water Desalination
abstract: Abstract The intensifying global water crisis calls for disruptive membrane technologies that transcend the long-standing permeability−selectivity trade-off in desalination. Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have emerged as promising nanoporous membrane platforms for modulating water and ion transport, yet research has largely fixated on sulfides and graphene. Here, we report monolayer molybdenum oxides (MoO2 and MoO3) as a promising candidate for 2D desalination nanoporous membrane, demonstrating how phase coordination and chalcogen chemistry govern water transport at the atomic scale. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that MoO3 nanopore outperforms benchmark 2H−MoS2 and graphene membranes by 20% and 65% in water flux, respectively, while sustaining ion rejection above 99%. Moreover, phase engineering of MoO2 polymorphs (1T and 1T′) provides enhanced permeability relative to conven
reason: MD simulations of water/ion transport in 2D molybdenum oxide nanopores for desalination.

title: Conducting Polymer-Based Nanofluidic Membranes for Osmotic Energy Conversion
abstract: Osmotic energy conversion (blue energy), serving as a sustainable marine renewable energy source, converts Gibbs free energy originating from salt concentration differences into electric power by virtue of ion-selective nanofluidic membranes. Conventional commercial ion-exchange polymer membranes suffer from inherent limitations, including low transmembrane flux, insufficient ion permselectivity, severe interfacial concentration polarization, poor salt tolerance, and unsatisfactory long-term structural stability. These drawbacks greatly restrict the energy conversion efficiency and large-scale engineering application of reverse electrodialysis (RED). Conductive polymers (CPs), mainly including polypyrrole (PPy), polyaniline (PANI), polythiophene (PTh), and their derivatives, possess the distinctive merits of tunable surface charge density and polarity, outstanding electronic conductivity
reason: Reviews conductive polymer nanofluidic membranes for high-efficiency osmotic energy conversion via reverse electrodialysis.

title: Biomimetic Nacre‐Inspired Nanofluidic Membranes with Concurrently Enhanced Ionic Conductivity and Mechanical Robustness
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional nanofluidic membranes are emerging as attractive functional materials for osmotic energy conversion, yet their practical implementation is hindered by the intrinsic trade‐off between ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness. Here, inspired by the hierarchical brick‐and‐mortar architecture of nacre and amino‐acid‐regulated ion transport in biological channels, a biomimetic hybrid nanofluidic membrane is developed by integrating glycine‐grafted poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA_Gly) into natural vermiculite via a simple vacuum‐assisted infiltration process. The grafted polymer simultaneously reinforces interlayer interactions and constructs bio‐inspired ion‐transport pathways while preserving the ordered lamellar framework. Consequently, the composite membrane achieves a nearly threefold enhancement in ionic conductivity together with a ∼3.5‐fold increase in tensile str
reason: Biomimetic 2D nanofluidic membranes enhance ionic conductivity and mechanical strength for osmotic energy harvesting.

title: Coupled Surface and Pore Diffusion of Neutral Organic Molecules in Nanopores
abstract: The transport of neutral organic molecules through nanoscale pores is central to a wide range of processes, yet the molecular factors governing their mobility remain difficult to predict. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations under a nonpolarizable force field to examine the diffusion of 1,4-dioxane, phenol, ethanol, and acetonitrile in anodic aluminum oxide nanopores with diameters of 4 and 8 nm. On the basis of the decay of molecule-wall potential energy and the molecular size, we establish a 1 nm boundary to separate surface-associated diffusion from pore-interior diffusion. Additionally, our simulation results show that surface diffusion is controlled by molecule-specific wall affinity and confinement-enhanced contact, whereas pore diffusion is governed by rotation-translation coupling. Molecules with higher polarity rotate faster, which reduces the persistent axial di
reason: MD simulations reveal coupled surface/pore diffusion mechanisms of neutral organics in nanopores, providing insights into diffusio-kinetic transport.

title: Harnessing Nonlinear Nanofluidic Rectification to Suppress Concentration Polarization
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
abstract: Abstract Electrokinetic transport in nanoscale systems has garnered significant interest because of its potential applications in desalination, molecular separation, and ion-selective devices. In particular, electroosmotic flow (EOF) through selective membranes offers a promising mechanism for voltage-driven reverse osmosis. However, a fundamental limitation arises from ion concentration polarization, which develops at the membrane extremities, creating a local voltage and increasing osmotic pressure that tend to limit the EOF. Through numerical simulations, we investigate the buildup of polarization at an osmotic diode interface under applied DC and AC electrostatic forces. We demonstrate that the concentration-induced polarization leads to a limitation of EOF efficiency and, under nonlinear rectified and AC fields, gives rise to complex depletion-polarization dynamics that fundamentall
reason: Simulates nonlinear nanofluidic rectification to suppress concentration polarization in electroosmotic flow.

title: Subnano-Confined Membrane Enables Efficient Brine Concentration and Salt Crystallization in Electrodialysis
abstract: Zero liquid discharge (ZLD) enables water and salt recovery while preventing secondary pollution, yet it is often energy-intensive and costly. Electrodialysis (ED), a widely employed technology for brine concentration in ZLD, is still in progress to overcome its insufficient concentrating ability due to unrestricted water transport through ion-exchange membranes. In this study, a tailored subnano-confined membrane (SCM) was prepared using a commercially available nanofiltration membrane and an ion exchange polymer. The ED system equipped with the SCM achieved a high concentration difference of 185 g L-1 NaCl in a single-stage operation and further produced crystallized NaCl at the third stage, offering a much simplified and effective concentrating process. The SCM featured ultralow water permeance, and the hydration number of ions passing through it was substantially reduced, which contr
reason: Subnano-confined membrane enhances electrodialysis brine concentration via ion dehydration, directly relevant to desalination and ion transport in nanochannels.

title: Biomimetic Nanofluidic Synapse with Programmable DNA Ion Gating for Neuromorphic Sensing and Computing
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Biological synapses process information through coupled neurotransmitter and ion fluxes, while conventional electron-based solid-state devices struggle to replicate this chemoelectrical signaling mechanism. Herein, we develop a biomimetic nanofluidic synapse designed for precise and programmable chemical gating. The platform integrates programmable DNA nanochannel (DN) arrays within a phospholipid multilayer assembled in situ on a robust anodic aluminum oxide membrane (termed DPAM), forming a bioinspired ion-gating interface. Crucially, DNA sequence programming enables plug-and-play adaptability for diverse neurotransmitters, while tuning DN dimensions customizes ion transport kinetics. As a prototypical example, glutamate-gated N-methyl-d-aspartate-like signaling is demonstrated to regulate transmembrane Ca2+ flux, successfully emulating fundamental synaptic plasticity. Furthermore, by
reason: DNA-programmable nanofluidic synapses emulate neurotransmitter-gated ion flux for neuromorphic computing and biosensing.

title: Water permeation through a nanogap between two disjoint carbon nanotubes: A comparison between charged and uncharged channels
venue: Physica E Low-dimensional Systems and Nanostructures
reason: Simulation compares water permeation in charged vs uncharged carbon nanotube nanogaps, relevant to electrokinetic nanochannel transport.

title: Active Ionic Fluxes Induce Symmetry Breaking in Charge-Patterned Nanochannels
abstract: Biological systems rely on autonomous modes of charge transport to transmit signals. Instead, conventional synthetic systems typically depend on external fields, such as voltage or pressure gradients, to induce transport, which limits their applicability. Here, we investigate nanochannels in which an electrolyte is confined by symmetric boundary patterns combining surface charge and active ionic fluxes. We show that the interplay between diffusion, electrostatics, and hydrodynamics in such nano-confined active-charged systems can trigger symmetry breaking above a critical active flux, leading to directed flow. Our results suggest that active-charged nanochannels can generate net flows of the order of hundreds of millimeters per second, opening pathways toward adaptable ionic devices and neuromorphic architectures.
reason: Active ionic fluxes induce symmetry breaking and directed flow in charge-patterned nanochannels.

title: Regulation of Ion Transport in Bioinspired Ion Channels: The Role of Cation–π Interactions
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
abstract: Abstract Cation–π interactions play important roles in regulating ion transport across the biological ion channels. Bioinspired ion channels (BINs) also employ cation–π interactions for various ion-related applications at the water–energy nexus, including ion separation and energy harvesting from natural water environment. However, the role of cation–π interactions in regulating ion transport remains relatively less investigated compared with other noncovalent interactions. Therefore, it is imperative to provide a detailed overview of recent advances in understanding of cation–π interactions for selective ion transport in BINs. In this review, the nature of cation–π interactions, function mechanism of prototypes, and ion-transport principles of BINs are presented. Four material classes─carbonaceous materials, organic materials, organic–inorganic hybrid materials, and composite materials
reason: Reviews cation-π interactions in bioinspired ion channels for selective ion transport, desalination, and osmotic energy conversion.

title: Oncogenic KRAS Regulates Secretion of Extracellular Vesicles and Surface Membrane Charge via Regulation of Phosphatidylserine in Pancreatic Cancer
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have the potential to be used as a liquid biopsy for cancer detection and treatment response assessment. Although the potential of EVs as disease-specific biomarkers has been promising, the rapid and specific enrichment of EVs from body fluids in a clinical setting remains challenging. To address this limitation, we developed a microfluidic electrophoresis (MEP) device for the label-free, charge-based enrichment of EVs from the serum of patients with pancreatic cancer (PaCa). We first validated the principle of charge-based cancer EV enrichment using cell-line-derived EVs, demonstrating that increased signaling through mutant Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homologue (KRAS), particularly KrasG12D, was associated with enhanced EV secretion and a shift toward more negative ζ-potential values. We then evaluated EVs derived from the serum of patients with PaCa
reason: Develops microfluidic electrophoresis device for charge-based extracellular vesicle enrichment from serum, direct biomedical electrokinetic application.

title: Amino Functionalization Significantly Boosts Nanopipette Sensitivity to Viscosity
abstract: Cytoplasmic viscosity dynamically varies when cells respond to physiological, pathological, or external stimuli. Precise analysis of these minimal fluctuations requires high sensitivity for real-time, high-fidelity monitoring. Herein, we developed an amino-functionalized nanopipette as a highly sensitive nanosensor for real-time dynamic monitoring of cytoplasmic viscosity in DU-145 human prostate cancer cells under both hypertonic and hypotonic conditions. Amino functionalization significantly enhanced the nanopipette's sensitivity to viscosity. Within a scanning window of -1.0 V to +1.0 V, it yielded a 189.56-fold increase at +1.0 V and up to a 17.96-fold improvement at their respective optimal applied potentials. This enhancement is primarily attributed to the increased interfacial charge density introduced by amino groups, which strengthens both the electrical double-layer effect and
reason: Develops amino-functionalized nanopipette sensor for real-time cytoplasmic viscosity monitoring via electroosmotic flow modulation.

title: Desalination Design Rules for Nanoporous 2D Materials: Low Edge Charges Sieve Ions, While Positive Edge Charges Exclude Boron
abstract: Abstract Molecular and ionic transport through nanopores in two-dimensional (2D) materials, which govern seawater desalination, are complex phenomena influenced by material chemistry, functional groups, and electrostatic interactions. We present a unified picture of nanoscale transport in 2D nanopores, demonstrating a pervasive principle valid across graphene, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2). That is, low edge charge effectively sieves ions, while positive edge charge excludes boron, which is regarded as the Achilles heel of seawater desalination. Quantum-mechanical calculations reveal that functional groups, such as hydrogen, hydroxyl, and oxo, modulate edge charges, tuning salt/boron rejection and water flux. Molecular simulations indicate that hydrogen-functionalized boron-terminated nanopores and oxygen-functionalized nitrogen-terminated hBN nanopores d
reason: Design rules for 2D nanopores reveal ion sieving mechanisms, directly relevant to nanopore ion transport and desalination.

title: A DNA Rotary Pump
abstract: Biological transmembrane molecular machines such as ATP synthase and flagellar motors couple chemical gradients to rotary motion and are essential to life. These biological pumps utilize energy and information ratchet mechanisms to overcome Brownian motion and directionally transport solutes across membranes. By contrast, fluid flow can be attained at the macroscopic level by continuous rotary motion. Here we explore the limits of rotary pump miniaturization by investigating the possibility of constructing a nanoscale Archimedes screw pump from a rapidly rotating DNA helix within a nanopore. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations revealed that MHz rotational frequencies would be needed to surpass Brownian motion. Net water and ion translocation was driven in the same direction, irrespective of the charge on the DNA or nanopore, which was consistent with a nanoscale screw-pump mechanism
reason: Simulates a DNA-based nanoscale rotary pump in a nanopore, revealing ion/water transport mechanisms and selectivity relevant to nanopore sensing and energy transduction.

title: Transmembrane potential across a charged nanochannel subjected to a salinity gradient
abstract: The transmembrane voltage, V_{i=0}, which is the potential drop required to nullify the electrical current (i=0), is a key characteristic of water desalination and energy harvesting systems that utilize macroscopically large nanoporous membranes, as well as for physiological ion channels subjected to asymmetric salt concentrations. To date, existing analytical expressions for V_{i=0} have been limited to simple scenarios under simplifying assumptions. In this work, we derive two expressions for V_{i=0}. First, we consider the much simpler scenario of two species. Then, we can consider an electrolyte composed of an arbitrary number of species. The difference in the models is that the latter solution utilizes an ad hoc assumption of a linear concentration profile, while the former solution does not require such an ad hoc assumption. However, to derive a closed-form solution, another assump
reason: Derives analytical expressions for transmembrane potential in charged nanochannels under salinity gradients, matching PNP simulations.

title: Surface Charge Modulation in Electroosmotic Mixing within Sinusoidal Wavy Rotating Micromixers
abstract: Abstract Electroosmotic mixing in a sinusoidal wavy micromixer subjected to rotational motion about an axis perpendicular to the plane of flow is numerically investigated, with particular emphasis on the combined effects of spatially modulated surface charge and Coriolis-induced secondary flows. A two-dimensional model is developed by solving the coupled Navier–Stokes, Poisson–Boltzmann, and species transport equations, and sinusoidally varying wall zeta potentials are prescribed with a controllable phase lag between the upper and lower walls. The influence of phase lag, electric double-layer thickness, rotation number, and Péclet number on flow structure and mixing performance is systematically examined. The results show that phase-lagged surface charge heterogeneity induces strong transverse perturbations that significantly modify the topology of electroosmotic flow and mixing efficie
reason: Numerical investigation of electroosmotic mixing in wavy micromixer with surface charge modulation and rotation, relevant to lab-on-chip mixing.

title: Electrohydrodynamic Origin of Direction-Dependent Conductive and Resistive Events in Nanopipettes
abstract: Understanding ion transport in nanopores is critical for optimizing nanopore-based sensing performance. Here, we report conductive events (CEs) during DNA translocation through conical nanopipettes under high and symmetric electrolyte conditions (1 M KCl), where conventional membrane nanopore systems generally exhibit resistive signals. Notably, these conductive signals show strong directional dependence, occurring only when λ-DNA translocates from the nanopipette interior to the external reservoir. To elucidate the origin and temporal characteristics of this behavior, we combine experiments with three-dimensional transient simulations based on the finite element method. The results reveal that conductive pulses arise from the coupled effects of ion enrichment and electrophoretic ion transport, governed by the interplay of applied bias, DNA surface charge, and electric double-layer effec
reason: Reveals electrohydrodynamic origin of direction-dependent conductive events in nanopipettes during DNA translocation.

title: Stress-induced ripping enables fabrication of nanopores with dimensions smaller than the resolution limit of the employed lithography
abstract: Nanopores in ultrathin membranes are central to single-molecule sensing, filtration, and energy conversion applications, yet fabrication of solid-state nanopores remains limited by fundamental trade-off between resolution, throughput, and tool complexity. Here, we report a scalable nanopore fabrication process that exploits stress-induced mechanical ripping to detach a fragment from a membrane with lateral dimensions in the nm-scale, forming pores with diameters down to the sub-10 nm regime, which is well below the resolution limit of the employed lithography. Using this approach, we demonstrate wafer-scale fabrication of nanopores at densities exceeding 10 5 pores per cm 2 in dielectric (HfO 2 ), semiconducting (SiGe), and metallic (Cr) membranes, including suspended HfO 2 membranes as thin as 2 nm. We demonstrate the utility of the fabricated nanopores for high-performance surface enha
reason: Novel stress-induced ripping fabricates sub-10 nm nanopores for single-molecule sensing and energy conversion.

title: Engineering of Spinel Channels for Selective Lithium Recovery from Simulated End-of-Life Lithium-Ion Battery Leachate
abstract: Abstract Surging global demand for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) creates an urgent imperative to recover critical materials from spent cells at scale. Here we integrate a spinel LiMn2O4 (LMO) ceramic membrane with a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) architecture enables self-sustaining ion-exchange. Water dissociation at the bipolar membrane generates a continuous proton flux that drives stoichiometric H+/Li+ exchange within the LMO lattice, providing in situ pH regulation without external eluent circulation. By decoupling lithium extraction from the discontinuous intercalation-deintercalation cycles inherent to conventional electrochemical approaches, this design enables continuous ion transport and faster extraction kinetics. Under optimized conditions, the system recovers a lithium recovery flux of 0.255 kg m–2 day–1 with a purity of 99.75%. This experimentally measured rate corr
reason: Ceramic membrane electrodialysis enables continuous lithium recovery via H+/Li+ exchange, relevant to ion-selective transport.

title: Investigation of Shielding Strategies to Mitigate Noise in Nanopore Recordings
authors: Y. M. Nuwan D. Y. Bandara
abstract: Shielding against electromagnetic interference (EMI), vibration, and mechanical noise is crucial for the reliable performance of sensitive electronics, especially in high-disturbance environments. While Faraday cages are ubiquitously used for this purpose, they are often implemented simply as metal boxes enclosing the measurement system without accounting for critical design factors such as skin depth. In this study, we investigated a range of factors to understand noise sources, coupling pathways, and systematic approaches for effective shielding beyond the common metal box approach, including the evaluation of power-line quality, grounding strategies for the Faraday cage, connectivity solutions to maintain Faraday cage integrity, and the relative positioning of the components in the measurement setup. Our findings have rendered the noise in the current measurements comparable to that o
reason: Develops EMI shielding strategies enabling high-bandwidth nanopore DNA translocation detection at low electrolyte concentrations.

title: Vinyl Functionalization of Ti3C2T x MXene Enables Grafting of Sulfonated Polyelectrolytes for High Salt Rejection in Forward Osmosis Desalination
abstract: MXene membranes are promising for aqueous separations but are fundamentally limited by swelling-induced loss of selectivity and structural instability. Here, we report, for the first time, vinyl functionalization of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets, which enables subsequent grafting of anionic polyelectrolyte networks within the lamellar nanochannels. Vinyltriethoxysilane is covalently anchored onto Ti3C2Tx to introduce polymerizable vinyl groups, transforming the MXene into a reactive platform for interfacial polymer integration. Each of the four sulfonated monomers (sodium p-styrene sulfonate, ammonium p-styrene sulfonate, 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid (AmPS), and 3-sulfopropyl methacrylate potassium salt) is subsequently grafted and crosslinked separately within the nanochannels to form hydrated, ion-exchange polymer networks. This approach converts swelling-prone Ti3C2Tx gallerie
reason: Develops MXene membranes with grafted polyelectrolytes for high salt rejection in forward osmosis.

title: Reactive walls enhance and prolong diffusiophoretic transport into dead-end channels
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Nonequilibrium colloidal transport mechanisms such as diffusiophoresis and Marangoni transport enable rapid and targeted delivery of colloids by exploiting in-situ or externally imposed chemical gradients, particularly in systems like dead-end pores where pressure-driven flow is ineffective. However, the duration of such transport is limited by how long the driving gradient persists. Here, we present a general strategy to prolong gradient-driven colloidal transport in dead-end channels using channel walls that preferentially adsorb the driving solute. Solute partitioning reduces the effective diffusivity of the cross-sectionally averaged solute field, slowing the evolution of the solute field without reducing particle diffusiophoresis. We demonstrate this concept in a controlled microfluidic system, where polystyrene particles migrate diffusiophoretically down sodium dodecyl sulfate grad
reason: Shows reactive walls prolong diffusiophoretic gradients in dead-end channels, enhancing colloidal transport control.

title: Monovalent Ion Selectivity Incomparability of Graphene Oxide Membrane in Different Separation Systems: A Microscopic Understanding
abstract: Precise monovalent ion sieving is essential for water treatment and resource recovery. However, ion selectivity reported from diffusion-based and electro-driven membrane processes is often inconsistent and difficult to reconcile due to unclear mechanistic understanding. Herein, combining experiments with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we reveal divergent microscopic mechanisms governing monovalent ion selectivity in graphene oxide (GO) nanochannels under different driving forces. Under concentration gradient-driven diffusion, ion selectivity is predominantly regulated by hydration-mediated effects (i.e., partial ion dehydration and dehydration-induced ion-membrane interactions) and cation-anion interaction. Specifically, in simulated defect-free GO nanochannel, Li+, with higher hydration energy and charge density than Na+, possesses a more intact hydration shell and stronger cation
reason: Shows driving-force-dependent ion selectivity mechanisms in graphene oxide nanochannels via experiments and MD simulations.

title: Mechanosensitive ion transport in hexagonal boron nitride nanopores
abstract: In biological systems, mechanical strain can trigger strong changes in ion conductance and signaling, yet in synthetic nanopores, achieving similar mechanosensitive behavior has been a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that subtle mechanical strain can induce strong modulation of ionic current in small hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanopores. Using hydrostatic pressure to apply small lateral strain to free-standing single-layer h-BN membranes featuring triangular sub-1-nm nanopores, we observed ion conductance modulation exceeding 1 30% under 0.5% strain. We attribute this response to the strain-dependent interplay of ionpore and ion-water interactions within the nanopore. The measured mechanosensitivity values also agreed strongly with those obtained from modeling of strain-tunable transport in ensembles of h-BN nanopores. These findings establish a framework for developing s
reason: Demonstrates strong mechanosensitive ion conductance modulation in h-BN nanopores, linking mechanical strain to transport.

title: Aromatic Peptide‐Enabled Cation‐π Engineering in Lamellar Nanochannels for Enhanced Cation Selectivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Ion selectivity is central to nanochannel membranes for ion separation, molecular recognition, and energy conversion. However, conventional membranes primarily rely on electrostatic repulsion to regulate ion selectivity; the short‐range and weak nature limits high selectivity. Herein, a cation‐π engineering strategy is proposed by intercalating aromatic peptides (APs) into sub‐nanometer graphene oxide (GO) channels. Systematic tuning of the π‐system with phenylalanine (F)‐, tyrosine (Y)‐, and tryptophan (W)‐based peptides reveals a dual role of cation‐π interactions, involving electrostatic attraction and cation confinement. Specifically, the Y‐based AP‐intercalated GO membrane achieves a cation transference number of 0.614, representing a 16.95% improvement over GO membrane, which is attributed to electrostatic attraction of π‐system toward cations. reason: Engineers cation-π interactions in GO nanochannels to enhance cation selectivity and osmotic power density.

title: pH-gated ion transport in covalent organic framework membranes functionalized with oxygen-containing groups
abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with pH-gated ion transport hold promise for smart nanofluidic devices, yet the regulatory mechanisms of different oxygen-containing functional groups remain poorly understood. Herein, we systematically investigate the pH-dependent ionic conductance of TpPa-R COF membranes (R = -SO3H, -COOH, -OH) across pH 3 to 11.5 using unmodified TpPa as a reference. All membranes exhibit nanofluidic transport with a U-shaped conductance profile as a function of pH. The neutral-pH conductance is governed by the effective surface charge density that drives counterion enrichment. Among the three modifications, the TpPa-SO3H membrane displays the broadest pH response and the highest conductance at both acidic and alkaline extremes. Notably, the TpPa-COOH membrane shows unexpectedly lower conductance than TpPa-OH at pH ≥ 5, which we attribute to hydration screeni
reason: pH-gated ion transport in COF nanochannels reveals surface charge effects.

title: Optimal electrokinetic energy conversion in a bi-layer nanochannel with slip-dependent zeta potential: A physics-constrained ANN-PSO framework
venue: International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer
reason: Optimizes electrokinetic energy conversion in bilayer nanochannels using physics-constrained machine learning, directly addressing energy harvesting.

title: Flow and transport characteristics of hydrogen in a square-spiral Knudsen pump with coupled thermal transpiration and Poiseuille flow
abstract: Gas transport driven by thermal transpiration under temperature gradients, known as a Knudsen pump, has shown strong potential in gas separation and delivery applications. However, its performance and operational stability are strongly affected by structural design, system integration, and manufacturing complexity, highlighting the need for efficient and manufacturable multi-stage configurations. In this study, a novel spiral-structured Knudsen pump is proposed. Within the microchannels, a temperature gradient drives gas from the low- to high-temperature region, inducing pressure rise and thermal transpiration. In the main channel, a pressure gradient drives gas from the high- to low-temperature region, forming Poiseuille flow. Numerical methods are employed to investigate the flow mechanisms, and the effects of varying the numbers of series and parallel microchannels on gas transmission
reason: Studies thermal transpiration in spiral microchannels for Knudsen pump, directly relevant to thermally driven transport.

title: Electrokinetic active grooves for liposome capture, confinement, trajectory analysis, and controlled release
abstract: Abstract Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are attractive candidates for minimally invasive disease monitoring. EV diagnostic signals often reside in low-abundant subpopulations, motivating single-vesicle measurements that can report distributions rather than ensemble averages. In practice, such assays rely on transient migration of a mobile vesicle through a detection region or performing cycled processing/measurement steps on vesicles permanently immobilized on surfaces via affinity-based capture. Single vesicle analysis would benefit from technologies that can combine characteristics of transient detection and surface immobilization to enable controlled capture, fixed time analysis and release of vesicles in a marker-neutral way. Here, we present electrokinetically active (RECON) grooves that provides low-voltage, programmable capture, timed retention, and release of nanoscale vesicles wit
reason: Electrokinetic grooves enable programmable capture, confinement, and release of nanoscale vesicles for single-vesicle analysis.

title: Valence-Selective Electrophoretic Transport in Neutral Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Understanding how confinement alters the transport of charged molecules is central to the advancement of separation, energy, and sensing technologies. Polyamines are small, linear molecules with ionizable groups, making them an ideal model for investigating charge transport in confinement beyond monatomic ions. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we investigate how molecular length, net charge, and charge placement affect the electrophoretic transport of polyamines through single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs). We find that nanometer-scale confinement reverses the mobility ordering observed in free solution -- in a CNT of radius 0.68 nm, spermine (q = +4) travels more slowly than ethylamine (q = +1), contrasting with the expected scaling of mobility with valence in bulk. reason: MD simulations reveal valence-selective electrophoretic transport of polyamines in carbon nanotubes due to confinement.

title: Mathematical Modeling of the Influence of Non-Uniform Electrical Conductivity of an Ion-Exchange Membrane on Salt Ion Transport in a Desalination Channel with Forced Convection
abstract: In this work, the influence of the electrical heterogeneity of the surface of an ion-exchange membrane on salt ion transport in a desalination channel with forced convection in the potentiodynamic mode is studied for the first time by the successful combined application of various mathematical methods: mathematical modeling based on a boundary value problem for the coupled system of the Navier–Stokes, Nernst–Planck, and Poisson equations; the finite element method for its numerical solution; an approximate analytical solution of the Stokes equations constructed by the method of images, in which the flow at the junction of the conducting and non-conducting regions is described as a flow induced by a point torque (rotlet); and a first-order relaxation model describing the growth of the vortex size. Since such problems have not been considered before, a new mathematical apparatus for their
reason: Models heteroelectroconvective vortices from membrane heterogeneity in desalination channels, relevant to coupled electrokinetic transport.

title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. reason: Janus nanoporous membrane achieves high power density in reverse electrodialysis via engineered nanochannels.

title: Thermo-hydrodynamic analysis of mixed driven flows in cylindrical microchannels considering slip-dependent zeta potential
venue: International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer
reason: Analyzes mixed thermo-hydrodynamic flows in microchannels with slip-dependent zeta potential, directly relevant to coupled electrokinetic and thermal transport.

title: Extreme slowdown of dsDNA and RNA:DNA hybrids in solid-state nanopores for LiCl concentrations above 4 mol/L
abstract: Abstract Solid-state nanopores enable single-molecule detection and characterization through ionic-current measurements, but rapid translocation can limit the resolution of molecular features. Here, we investigated the translocation of 7.2 kb dsDNA and 3.3 kb RNA:DNA hybrids at LiCl concentrations extending to 7 mol/L. Both constructs exhibited a substantial increase of ≳ 500% in mean translocation time when increasing LiCl concentration from 2–3 M to 7 M . We also observed a decrease in translocation frequency at increasing LiCl concentration. Both observations indicate a reduction in the effective electric driving force. Further analysis indicates a substantial decrease in the relative width of secondary peaks induced by labels on the molecule. Our results show that increasing salt concentration beyond 4 mol/L is an accessible way for increasing translocation time in solid-state nanopo
reason: Shows extreme DNA slowdown in solid-state nanopores at high LiCl concentrations, improving translocation time for sensing.

title: Electrokinetic flow of fluids with pressure-dependent viscosity and slip-dependent zeta potential
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the electrokinetic flow and electrokinetic energy conversion efficiency(EKEC) of fluids characterized by pressure-dependent (P.D.) viscosity and slip-dependent (S.D.) zeta potential within a slip channel. Using the exponential pressure-viscosity relationship, we derive the electrokinetic flow characteristics of the fluid by solving the continuity and two-dimensional momentum equations with the perturbation method. A systematic study is then conducted on the influence of S.D. zeta potential and the effect of P.D. viscosity on the pressure, viscosity, velocity, streaming potential, and electrokinetic energy conversion efficiency. The results show that the P.D. viscosity effect increases the pressure and the fluid viscosity, but reduces the electrokinetic energy conversion efficiency. reason: Theoretical study of electrokinetic flow and energy conversion efficiency with pressure-dependent viscosity and slip-dependent zeta potential.

title: Enzymatically Active Liposomal Nanobots for the Penetration of Intercellular and Intracellular Barriers
abstract: Delivery systems for nanomedicine are critical, however, they are restricted by intercellular and intracellular barriers including lysosomal sequestration after cellular uptake, that impede penetration from the tissue to the subcellular level. Here, we report a liposomal nanobot with enzymatic propulsion and drug-payload capabilities that exhibits tumor microenvironment responsiveness and active penetration, enabling intracellular transport and active lysosomal escape. This nanobot arises from phase-separated vesicles of liposome and bacterial outer membrane vesicles that possess doxorubicin-encapsulation capability and are asymmetrically functionalized with glucose oxidase to form a Janus catalytic interface for self-diffusiophoresis in the presence of glucose. Under mildly acidic conditions, these nanobots display enhanced motility and chemotactic migration toward acidic regions, lever
reason: Enzymatic nanobots use self-diffusiophoresis for active transport across biological barriers.

title: Asymmetric Induced-Charge Electroosmotic Flows around Partially Conducting Cylinders in Shear-Thinning Fluids
abstract: Abstract In this two-dimensional computational study, induced-charge electroosmosis (ICEO) around a half-conducting Janus cylinder immersed in a power-law shear-thinning electrolyte is considered within a fully coupled Poisson–Nernst–Planck–Stokes (PNP-Stokes) formulation, with the selected range of the flow-behavior index providing a systematic framework to investigate the influence of shear-dependent viscosity on ICEO-induced transport. The asymmetric surface conductivity of the Janus cylinder breaks the classical dipolar symmetry of ICEO, producing localized polarization zones, unequal counter-rotating vortices, and strongly modified azimuthal velocity distributions. Incorporation of a power-law rheological model demonstrates that shear-thinning behavior significantly amplifies the induced near-surface flow, enlarges recirculation regions, and enhances convective ion transport. reason: Simulates asymmetric ICEO flows around Janus cylinders in shear-thinning fluids, showing enhanced mixing.

title: Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis for Nutrients Separation and Recovery from Wastewater
abstract: Bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) is an electro-membrane separation technology used for over 20 years to treat liquid wastes, including wastewater from various industrial processes, municipal wastewater, and animal farms. This technology has been developed for its ability to dissociate H2O into H+ and OH− ions and to convert cations and anions in the feed solution into bases and acids, respectively, by applying an electrical potential. In comparison with alternative treatment technologies, BMED has some advantages, such as no need for chemical reagents, high degrees of efficiency, and straightforward operational procedures. However, BMED has been limited by a high level of preparation expense for BMs, membrane deposition, and ion loss during operation. This review mainly describes the principles and designs of BMED, their compositions along with their advantages and disadvantages,
reason: Reviews bipolar membrane electrodialysis for nutrient recovery, directly relevant to electrodialysis and ion transport.

title: Linking Flow-Derived Local Slip Lengths to Force-Derived Effective Slip Lengths in Nanogaps
abstract: Abstract A quantitative understanding of interfacial slip is important for determining boundary conditions and evaluating fluid-flow characteristics in nanogaps relevant to fluidic devices and precision micromechanical systems. Interfacial slip has been conventionally evaluated in terms of the slip length derived from squeeze-force measurements, in which the hydrodynamic force generated within the narrowing gap between solid surfaces is compared with a hydrodynamic model assuming a spatially constant slip length. However, the slip length may depend on local flow conditions and may vary spatially within nanogaps. The relationship between such spatially distributed local slip lengths and the force-derived constant slip lengths remains unclear. reason: Experimental study linking local and effective slip lengths in nanogaps, crucial for nanoscale fluid transport modeling.

title: Enhanced reverse electrodialysis performance using modified profiled ion-exchange membranes with reduced profile height and increased profile spacing
abstract: Improving the power generation performance of reverse electrodialysis (RED) requires both a high open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) and low internal resistance ( R int ). In this study, a profiled ion-exchange membrane (PF membrane) with a profile height of 90 μm, a profile spacing of 2.0 mm and an inclination angle of 9° was fabricated and applied to a RED stack with an intermembrane distance of 180 μm. The performance of the modified PF membrane was evaluated and compared with that of a flat membrane with an intermembrane distance of 180 μm and a previously reported PF membrane with an intermembrane distance of 380 μm. Although the modified PF membrane exhibited a slightly lower V OC than the flat membrane, it showed a substantial reduction in R int . reason: Profiled ion-exchange membranes enhance reverse electrodialysis power density; direct application for energy harvesting.

title: Reduced thermodynamic representation of multicomponent hypersaline electrolytes and its electrochemical projection through reverse electrodialysis
abstract: Reverse electrodialysis (RED) open-circuit voltage reflects the electrochemical potential difference between electrolyte streams, but its interpretation is complicated in hypersaline mixtures by strong solution non-ideality and membrane effects. Here, the ion-specific activity state of a multicomponent brine is reduced to a dimensionless descriptor, Λ multi , using charge-equivalent weighting. The South Aral Sea is used as the reference system, with activities in both streams calculated using the same Pitzer-based multicomponent model. At 298.15 K, the charge-balanced brine has an ionic strength of 6.6705 mol kg −1 . Its calculated Λ multi is 7.0992, compared with an ideal value of 8.6843, corresponding to an 18.3% reduction. reason: Models non-ideal thermodynamics of hypersaline brines for reverse electrodialysis voltage prediction, relevant to energy harvesting.

title: Single-molecule nanopore sensing across a liquid-solid interface
abstract: Abstract Single-molecule nanopore sensing conventionally relies on the translocation of molecules between two liquid electrolyte chambers separated by a nanopore. Here, we challenge this assumption and demonstrate that molecules can translocate through a solid-state nanopore from a liquid into a solid while retaining single-molecule resolution. This is enabled by a uniquely formulated solid polymer electrolyte (solid PE) that directly replaces the conventional liquid trans chamber. We carried out a comprehensive physicochemical characterization of the solid PE, revealing a hygroscopic, semicrystalline material that is mechanically stable in the solid state and ionically conductive. These properties enable the operation of solid-state nanopores with a solid trans chamber, allowing the detection of a diverse range of biomolecules, including double-stranded DNA, DNA nanostructures and ribos
reason: Demonstrates single-molecule nanopore sensing with solid polymer electrolyte trans chamber, enhancing sensitivity and enabling diverse biomolecule detection.

title: Ionic Nano‐Engineering of Wood Cell Walls for High‐Performance Marine Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanofluidic systems hold great promise for water treatment and blue energy harvesting. However, fabricating natural‐based nanofluidic materials that simultaneously deliver tunable channel orientation, high charge density, and robust mechanical at scale remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate a wood nanofluidic platform enabled by ionic nano‐engineering of the wood cell wall, involving ionized cell‐wall scaffold reconstruction and in situ nanopolymer polymerization. Periodate oxidation followed by Schiff‐base coupling grafts positively charged ─NH 2 functionalities onto the cellulose skeleton, converting oxidized wood from negatively charged (ζ = −16.5 mV) to positively charged (ζ = +33.5 mV). reason: Engineers charged nanochannels in wood for high-performance salinity-gradient energy harvesting.

title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. reason: Identifies nanochannel dynamics as key to enhancing molecular transport and selectivity under confinement.

title: Thermal management of electrothermal microchannels: A dual-chip approach for biocompatible fluid pumping
abstract: While electrothermal (ET) pumping is a highly promising technique for microfluidic actuation, its application in biofluids is often restricted by the maximum allowable temperature to prevent thermal damage to biological samples. To overcome this limitation, this study investigates the integration and parametric optimization of cooling chips alongside conventional heating chips within ET microchannels. Utilizing a newly developed numerical finite volume solver in OpenFOAM, the coupled electrical, thermal, and hydrodynamic governing equations are resolved to systematically analyze the effects of chip geometry, placement, and channel dimensions. reason: Investigates electrothermal pumping with integrated cooling for biocompatible microfluidics, directly relevant to thermally driven transport.

title: Crown Ether-Functionalized Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Monovalent Cation Separation
abstract: Membrane-based separation offers a highly promising paradigm for the precise extraction of monovalent cations, which is critical for bioinspired engineering and advanced ion-separation applications. However, efficient discrimination among these cations remains profoundly challenging owing to their nearly identical valence states and comparable subnanometer hydrated diameters. Herein, we report the rational design and fabrication of crown ether (CE)-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that achieve efficient mono/monovalent cation separation while maintaining rapid ion transport. The integration of CE moieties into the framework architectures plays a dual role: narrowing the channels to the angstrom scale while simultaneously serving as specific recognition sites for target cations through host-guest interactions. title: Yielding-dependent Taylor dispersion in electrokinetic-magnetohydrodynamic Casson microflows
abstract: Longitudinal dispersion in a yielding fluid depends on the velocity distribution and on how the flow is maintained. We study a neutral tracer in pressure-assisted electrokinetic and magnetohydrodynamic flow of a Casson fluid through a slit microchannel. The nonlinear stress and velocity equations determine the yielded layers, the unyielded core and the axial flow. Mei's multiple-scale homogenization of the advection-diffusion equation then separates transverse relaxation, mean drift and longitudinal spreading, yielding the Taylor-Aris auxiliary problem and effective diffusivity. An exact pressure-driven solution gives cubic decay of the mean velocity and eighth-power decay of the dispersion enhancement near flow arrest. title: Interfacial control and evaporation pinning of nanocapillary filling from ambient to serpentinization temperatures
abstract: Abstract Fluid transport in nanometer-scale channels underlies nanofluidic technologies and geological systems, yet measured capillary filling rates in hydrophilic channels are often far slower than classical theory predicts. Here we show, using a coupled flow model based on classical density functional theory combining hydrodynamics, electrokinetics and capillarity, that electrokinetic resistance and locally elevated viscosity near the channel walls jointly suppress flow, capturing the measured slowdown across independent experiments. title: Interfacially Regulated MXene‐Based Nanocomposite Membranes for Highly Selective Ion Transport and Salinity Gradient Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high ion selectivity, low membrane resistance, and long‐term stability remains a key challenge in developing two‐dimensional nanomaterial polymer composite membranes, where interfacial interactions critically influence membrane structure and ion transport. Here, we report interfacially regulated MXene‐based nanocomposite membranes in which humic acid (HA) mediates interactions between Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix. Structural characterization together with molecular dynamics simulations indicates that HA incorporation modifies MXene organization and interfacial interactions within the membrane, which are associated with enhanced ion‐transport properties. title: Janus Membranes for Osmotic Energy Harvesting and Flow Capacitive Deionization
abstract: The conversion of osmotic energy from salinity gradients into electricity offers a sustainable and low‐intermittency source of clean power, capable of complementing existing energy systems. Membrane properties are central to the efficiency of such energy conversion; however, conventional ion‐exchange membranes often suffer from high internal resistance and limited performance. In this work, we report a Janus membrane engineered from a microporous sulfonated poly(ether sulfone) base coated with a thin, nano‐porous, positively charged crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol)–poly(ethyleneimine) layer. The asymmetric architecture promotes directional ion transport, selectivity, and reduced resistance, leading to high osmotic energy harvesting. reason: Develops Janus membrane for osmotic energy harvesting and capacitive deionization, directly relevant to energy harvesting and desalination.

title: Label‐Free YaxAB Nanopore Fingerprinting of Cancer‐Associated Single‐Residue Bcl‐xL Variants
abstract: Resolving cancer-associated protein variants remains difficult when variants share similar molecular masses and folded structures. Conventional assays often require labels or provide ensemble-averaged readouts, limiting their ability to resolve subtle variant differences. Here, a YaxAB nanopore workflow is presented for label-free single-molecule current fingerprinting of wild-type Bcl-xL and the cancer-associated single-residue variants N136K and R165W. Individual Bcl-xL proteins were electro-osmotically trapped within the funnel-shaped YaxAB lumen, where they generated characteristic ionic-current events. These events formed reproducible, analyte-specific event populations in normalized current blockade and current noise space, resolving wild-type Bcl-xL, N136K, and R165W as distinct single-molecule current fingerprints. reason: Uses YaxAB nanopore for label-free protein fingerprinting via electro-osmotic trapping and ionic current blockade, advancing nanopore sensing.

title: Laser-induced fluorescence temperature mapping in microfluidics: Calibration strategy and application to AC electrothermal microflows
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
abstract: This paper presents a non-invasive laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) approach for temperature mapping in microfluidic chambers and then applies it to an alternating-current electrothermal (ACET) flow considered as a representative electro-microfluidic test case. Temperature mapping remains difficult when the device height is only a few hundred micrometers and when intrusive probes would disturb either the hydrodynamic field or the applied electric field. Rhodamine B dissolved in physiological saline is therefore characterized independently in absorbance and fluorescence before being used as a temperature-sensitive tracer. title: An autonomous regenerative bioelectronic dressing powered by wound exudate for high-quality skin repair
abstract: Endogenous electric field (EF) plays a crucial role in the wound healing process, yet conventional electrical stimulation strategies remain constrained by their dependence on bulky external power supplies. Herein, we report a bilayer electrogenerative smart dressing (B-ESD) that generates a self-sustained EF through a robust streaming potential induced by unidirectional pumping of wound exudate. This biofluid-driven mechanism successfully amplified the attenuated wound potential from 343.8 to 921.0 mV without requiring any external power source. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated that this self-sustained EF mitigated acute inflammation, accelerated fibroblast migration, and promoted highly organized collagen deposition. title: Nonmonotonic hydration dependence of ionic transport in atomically thin MnO 2 sheets
abstract: The interlamellar space in van der Waals materials has served as a test bed for studies of strongly confined fluid and ion transport. Despite theoretical and experimental progress, it remains unclear how electrostatic correlations arising from interactions between the confined, hydrated ions and the substrate layer can be reconciled with non-equilibrium ionic transport and the substrate's morphological response. Here, we investigate field-driven ionic conduction in sodium- and water-intercalated layered manganese oxides ($\mathrm{MnO_2}$), a self-intercalated metal oxide nanofluidic system, as a model intrinsically-intercalated van der Waals solid, using nonequilibrium all-atom molecular dynamics simulations that explicitly capture ion-water correlations and layer morphology. title: Ion transport and thermodynamics in a cation exchange membrane under experimentally relevant conditions: an atomistic study
abstract: Ion exchange membranes are important in energy and separation technologies. Molecular-level simulations of ion transport and thermodynamic behaviour within these materials exist, but these are often disconnected from experimental data. In this work, atomistic molecular dynamic simulations were performed to investigate a hydrated sulfonated polystyrene-based cation exchange membrane equilibrated with three electrolytes (i.e., LiCl, NaCl, and KCl), under experimentally relevant conditions (i.e. 0.1 M - 1.0 M). The simulations used experimentally measured water uptake and ion exchange capacity to provide key membrane-phase properties consistent with experimental observations, including water volume fractions and counterion concentrations. title: Dynamics of charge fluctuations in nanocapacitors: Effects of salt concentration and electrode metallicity from Brownian dynamics
abstract: Electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) rely on the dynamical response of confined electrolytes to store and release charge, yet the interplay between ion transport, electrostatic interactions, and electrode metallicity remains poorly understood at the nanoscale. In this work, we develop a comprehensive Brownian dynamics framework to compute the frequency-dependent admittance of nanocapacitors, explicitly accounting for salt concentration and the finite screening length of electrodes (modeled via Thomas-Fermi theory). We derive the fluctuation-dissipation relation connecting the dynamics of equilibrium charge fluctuations to the linear response of the system quantified by the frequency-dependent admittance. title: pH-responsive nanopores enable programmable transmembrane potential
abstract: Biological ion channels achieve highly selective, ultrafast ion transport through stimulus-responsive gating, in which conformational changes triggered by chemical cues such as pH that modulate channel permeability with exquisite precision. Replicating this coupled chemical-structural functionality in synthetic membranes remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for scalable platforms relevant to energy harvesting, desalination, and chemical sensing. Here, we report a bioinspired polymer-metal-organic framework (MOF) composite membrane in which an amino acid (histidine) functionalized MOF nanopores serve as synthetic proton-gated anion channel. The histidine modified, spatially confined ion transport pathway exhibited selective Cl- diffusion at pH 4, enabling pH programmable control of transmembrane potential. title: Outside Front Cover: Rational Molecular Design to Improve Digital Polymer Readout in Aerolysin‐Based Nanopore Sequencing
abstract: The cover depicts polymers as colourful molecular “beads” threading through an aerolysin nanopore embedded in a lipid membrane. Rationally designed monomers, represented by distinct colours and digital symbols, produce characteristic translocation signals. By tuning polymer architecture and pore interactions, molecular structures can be translated into reliable digital information at the single-molecule level. title: Negative Chemotaxis of Urease‐Functionalized Polymeric Microcapsules
abstract: Enzyme-driven micromotors provide a promising platform for mimicking biological chemotaxis and for developing responsive materials. We recently developed a method to make cell-sized asymmetric urease-functionalized poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microcapsules that are highly motile in the presence of urea. Here, we investigate the chemotactic behavior of these microcapsules in urea gradients in a chemotaxis chamber. We demonstrate that urease-functionalized microcapsules exhibit negative chemotaxis, migrating down urea gradients over a wide range of gradient magnitudes. title: Molecular dynamics insights into water flux and salt rejection in nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes incorporated with Ag nanoparticles for capacitive deionization
abstract: Capacitive deionization (CDI) is an environmentally friendly and energy-efficient method for saline water desalination; however, conventional carbon-based electrodes are often limited by low salt adsorption capacity (SAC). In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to investigate the desalination performance of nitrogen-doped carbon nanotube (N-CNT) and silver-encapsulated N-CNT (Ag/N-CNT) electrodes under pressure-driven flow and varying electric field strengths. The results show that water flux is strongly field-dependent in both systems, with Ag/N-CNT exhibiting significantly higher flux due to the presence of Ag nanoparticles. title: Effects of Ion Partitioning and Ion Steric on Electroosmotic Flow of Power-Law Fluids in Soft Nanochannels with Similar/Dissimilar Polyelectrolyte Layers
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the electroosmotic flow (EOF) of a power-law fluid through an asymmetric soft nanochannel, accounting for ion steric and ion partitioning effects. title: Harnessing electrothermo-convection of non-Newtonian fluids for advanced shipboard electronics cooling
venue: Journal of Ocean Engineering and Science
abstract: Thermal management of high-power-density electronics constitutes a critical bottleneck in advanced ship propulsion systems, motivating active cooling strategies beyond conventional methods. This study numerically investigates electrothermo-convection (ETC) in power-law non-Newtonian dielectric fluids within a parallel-plate configuration, a canonical model for compact shipboard heat sinks. A coupled multiphysics framework integrating fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and electrohydrodynamics is formulated, incorporating ion conduction with field-enhanced dissociation. title: Interfacial electrostatics of confined aqueous electrolytes: A new frontier for tuning water permeability and ion selectivity
abstract: The behavior of water and salt ions in nanoscale environments departs fundamentally from bulk expectations, with important consequences for membrane separations, biological ion channels, and electrochemical energy technologies. A key origin of these departures is the pronounced suppression and anisotropy of the dielectric response of water arising from confinement-induced constraints on water ordering. title: A nanoscale flow characterization model based on the apparent boundary layer
abstract: The incompatibility between macroscopic continuum assumptions and microscopic molecular mechanisms remains a key challenge in nanoscale flow modeling. To address this issue, this work introduces the concept of an apparent boundary layer, with its thickness denoted as happ. The model is constructed by combining a short-range interaction viscosity model with a fixed-partition viscosity model under flow conservation constraints. The parameter happ is determined through numerical solution of the resulting implicit equation. After model validation, the flow behavior within a single nanopore is systematically analyzed. title: Slippery boundaries enhance trapping of catalytic micromotors
abstract: The locomotion of catalytic micromotors is strongly influenced by nearby boundaries, where hydrodynamic and chemical interactions collectively govern their dynamics. By incorporating hydrodynamic slip into the theoretical framework, we capture the effects of nearby surface wettability on the dynamics of a self-diffusiophoretic micromotor. title: Synergistic Regulation of Heat and Ion Transport in Horizontal Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Efficient Low‑Grade Heat Harvesting
abstract: Selective ion thermodiffusion within nanofluidic membranes offers a promising route for low-grade heat harvesting. However, their thermoelectric performance often suffers from parasitic heat conduction across the thin membrane, which rapidly dissipates the thermal driving force. This calls for an integrated strategy that simultaneously regulates ion transport and heat conduction. abstract: One of the most challenging issues in nanofluidic systems is the development of highly efficient desalination membranes that can simultaneously achieve high water permeability and ion selectivity. title: Charge-neutral nanoporous membrane enables one-step electrodialytic dye/salt fractionation
abstract: Abstract Sustainable high-salinity dye-containing wastewater management demands a paradigm shift from conventional pollutant removal to circular resource recovery. Herein, we report a bio-inspired, electro-driven nanoporous membrane as a high-performance anion-conducting platform for one-step electrodialytic separation. Through co-deposition of dopamine and polyethyleneimine, we achieved precise sub-nanometer regulation of membrane properties, including tunable pore sizes (from 1.00 nm to 0.51 nm), near-zero surface charge (from −10.2 mV to −0.9 mV), and reduced electrical resistance (from 6.15 to 3.31 Ω·cm 2 ), enabling an optimal balance between dye rejection and ion transport. title: Ion Size-Dependent Flow Modulation and Selectivity in Polyelectrolyte Grafted Nanochannels under Combined Electroosmotic and Pressure-Driven Transport
abstract: Abstract We propose a detailed study of the electroosmotic and pressure-driven flow of power-law fluids through soft nanochannels grafted with polyelectrolyte layers (PELs). A power-law model represents the fluid’s non-Newtonian rheology, allowing for the consistent treatment of both shear-thinning and shear-thickening behaviours under typical nanochannel configurations. reason: Models electroosmotic and pressure-driven flow in polyelectrolyte-grafted nanochannels with ion size effects and non-Newtonian rheology.

title: Carbonyl‐Enriched Nonionic Covalent Organic Framework Nanochannels for High‐Salinity Ionic Thermoelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐salinity electrolytes coupled with low‐grade heat offer an attractive opportunity for ionic thermoelectric conversion, yet conventional fixed‐charge membranes rapidly lose ion permselectivity in concentrated media because Donnan exclusion is strongly screened. Here, we report an isoreticular series of nonionic covalent organic framework membranes with comparable one‐dimensional nanochannels but systematically varied pore‐wall oxygen chemistry. title: Electrically Tunable Selectivity Enhancement Overcomes the Permeability-Selectivity Trade-off in Two-dimensional Nanofluidic Channels
abstract: Abstract Membrane-based desalination and other separation processes are suffering from a ubiquitous, pernicious trade-off between selectivity and permeability, i.e., high selectivity comes at the expense of reduced permeability, and vice versa. Here we show that applying an external electric field can drastically enhance the salt rejection rate of two-dimensional nanofluidic channels from approximately 84%—a level unsuitable for commercial use—to as high as 99.5%, while leaving the water flow rate unaffected, thereby overcoming the permeability-selectivity trade-off. abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT)-based ionic nanochannels offer a powerful platform for controlling ion transport at the nanoscale, enabling highly sensitive biosensing modalities based on molecularly gated ion transport. Devices fabricated via CVD growth, mechanical transfer, and microfabrication of integrated reservoirs and electrodes exhibit stable and reproducible ionic transport in KCl electrolytes. title: IR Light Induces a Switch of Protein Translocation Direction from Electroosmotic to Electrophoretic in Quartz Nanopore Sensing

abstract: Single-molecule nanopore sensing provides a high-resolution, label-free platform to probe biomolecular dynamics and transport phenomena. title: Multi‐Stimuli Responsive Angstrom‐Scale Two‐Dimensional Channels of Natural Layered Materials
abstract: Biological ion channels are nature's wonders that regulate complex and multifunctional molecular mechanisms in living things. Emulating such multifunctionality in artificial systems remains a formidable challenge due to the limitations in achieving concurrent multi-stimuli responsiveness. Here, we report biomimetic and multi-responsive two-dimensional (2D) ion channels with Angstrom (Å)-scale channel heights, naturally formed within the interlayer galleries of vermiculite (VM) clay, which inherently possesses negatively charged surfaces. authors: Y. M. Nuwan D. Y. Bandara
abstract: DNA translocation through solid-state nanopores has been investigated extensively as a powerful platform for label-free and single-molecule sensing. In this study, we investigate the effects of visible light on DNA molecules using quartz nanopipettes—low-noise solid-state nanopores with a tapered geometry. title: Bioinspired Oxygen Functional Group Density Governs Hydrovoltaic Energy Harvesting for Soil–Moisture–Driven Plant Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrovoltaic generators convert ambient water flow into electricity, yet their power output has plateaued for lack of a quantitative link between surface chemistry and electrokinetic performance. title: Momentum-scalar coupled turbulence with anomalous momentum and scalar diffusions. Part 2: With short-range external force and implementation in electrokinetic turbulence
abstract: We extend the generalized anomalous diffusion framework established in Part 1 to the short-range forcing regime ($β>2/3$), where the multiscale-force dominated (MFD) subrange is intercalated after the inertial subrange, competing directly with the dissipation ranges. title: Architecting Biomimetic Proton Channels in Membranes for Energy and Environment Applications
abstract: Biological proton channels enable rapid and perfectly selective proton transport through highly confined and functionalized structures. Inspired by these natural systems, this review first elucidates the fundamental transport mechanisms underlying biological proton channels (e.g., Hv1, M2), emphasizing the role of hydrogen bonding networks and the Grotthuss mechanism. title: Dynamic Hydration Gating Enables Terahertz Frequency-Selective Na+ Transport under Nanoconfinement
abstract: Abstract Frequency-selective regulation of ion channels by terahertz fields is often associated with the response of water, yet how hydration dynamics determine ion-transport outcomes remains unclear. title: Tailoring Sub‐Nanochannels and Ion‐Imprinted Functionality of Palygorskite‐Derived Membranes for Desalination and Lithium‐ion Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanofiltration membranes with tailorable sub‐1‐nm channels are essential for desalination and ion separation, yet scalable and eco‐friendly fabrication of function‐switchable membranes remains a formidable challenge. abstract: Nanofluidic memristors, exploiting ion transport in nanochannels, hold promise for neuromorphic applications. title: Enhanced performance of a Reverse Electrodialysis stack for hydrogen and electricity cogeneration with tailored low-resistance ion-conductive spacers
abstract: Reverse electrodialysis (RED) is a promising technology for harnessing salinity gradient energy (SGE) to generate electricity and hydrogen. abstract: ABSTRACT Classical nanofluidic ion transport predominantly relies on fixed surface charges for selectivity. title: Microfluidic Sample Compartmentalization for Biomolecular Concentration Quantification Using a Nanopore Sensor
abstract: Determination of the concentration of a biomolecule in a sample is a fundamental measurement in analytical chemistry and central to many diagnostic applications. title: Improving Ionic Current Rectification in Misaligned Janus Bilayer Nanoporous Graphene through Tuning Electric Field Direction
abstract: In recent years, nanoporous graphene has shown great potential in nanofluidic devices and ion separation applications. However, in multilayer architectures, pore misalignment significantly suppresses ion transport efficiency, and its underlying mechanism remains insufficiently understood. To address this issue, this study employs molecular dynamics simulations to systematically examine the effect of pore alignment and electric field direction on ionic current rectification (ICR) in Janus bilayer nanoporous graphene (NPG). The results show that, with increasing pore offset, ions become strongly enriched in the NPG interlayer region, forming a localized high-concentration environment that hinders ion migration and induces an ICR inversion. title: Multifunctional Boron Nitride/Sodium Alginate Lamellar Membranes for Robust Osmotic Energy Harvesting and Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract Osmotic energy, derived from salinity-gradient-driven mixing, is a clean renewable resource that may help address energy and environmental challenges. Ion-exchange membranes incorporating two-dimensional (2D) materials are attractive for reverse electrodialysis, yet manufacturing large-area membranes with low transport resistance remains challenging. In this work, 2D boron nitride (BN)/sodium alginate (SA) composite membranes are fabricated through polymer-assisted ball-milling exfoliation and doctor-blade casting; subsequent Ca2+-induced ionic crosslinking of SA is used to strengthen their stability in water. The as-prepared membranes possess a mesoscopic lamellar architecture that supports ion migration. title: Molecular dynamics validation of shear-dependent nonlinear slip boundary condition for water
abstract: The classical no-slip boundary condition has long served as a foundational assumption in continuum fluid mechanics; however, it is known to break down in microscale and high-shear flows where interfacial slip becomes significant. Nonlinear slip models proposed by Thompson and Troian, and later generalized by Thalakkottor and Mohseni, demonstrated that slip length is not constant but increases nonlinearly with shear rate. Previous validations of these models have primarily relied on monatomic Lennard-Jones (LJ) fluids, limiting their applicability to realistic liquids. title: NanoConfinementChat: A Domain-Specific Large Language Model for Mechanistic Interpretation of Nanoconfined Water and Ion Transport in Membrane Nanochannels
abstract: Nanoconfined water and ion transport determines permeability and selectivity in membrane nanochannels, yet the relevant mechanisms are dispersed across material systems, molecular simulations, and theoretical studies, hindering systematic mechanism-oriented knowledge synthesis. Here, we develop NanoConfinementChat, a domain-specific large language model (LLM) for analyzing transport mechanisms in ion-selective membrane nanochannels. A curated corpus of 518 papers was used to construct 8500 mechanism-oriented instruction-answer pairs for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module was further integrated for literature grounding and source tracing, and model performance was assessed using a 90-question gold-point benchmark.
