reason: Develops LLM for mechanistic interpretation of nanoconfined water/ion transport in nanochannels, directly relevant to fundamental transport physics.

title: Protein Phase Transition Engineering of Nanochannels: A Stepwise Functionalization Strategy for Sequential Ultrasensitive Metal Ion Detection
abstract: Water-soluble heavy metal ions pose persistent threats to ecosystems and human health, necessitating highly sensitive and selective detection strategies. Herein, we report a nanochannel sensing platform for sequential ion detection, constructed via a protein-phase-transition-induced in situ interface engineering strategy. Bovine serum albumin (BSA) is converted into phase-transited BSA (PTB) through tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP)-mediated disulfide bond cleavage, forming a uniform PTB layer within conical nanochannels. The abundant thiol (-SH) groups on PTB enable ultrasensitive Hg2+ detection via strong Hg-S interactions, achieving an exceptionally low detection limit of 2.26 × 10-14 M. abstract: Herein, we investigate a coulometric nanomembrane-based ISE integrated into a microfluidic cell pursuing the absolute analysis of potassium ions (K+), selected as a model example. The sensor consisted of a glass substrate coated with the conducting polymer poly(3-octylthiophene) (POT) and a nanometer-sized, potassium-selective membrane casted on top. In the microfluidic cell, the sample is confined to a thin-layer domain being sandwiched between the working electrode and the counter/reference electrode. Two electrochemical protocols are developed toward exhaustive ion transfer at the membrane-sample interface: (i) an anodic mode, where K+ is first accumulated in the membrane and then released to the sample, and (ii) a cathodic mode, where ion release from the membrane is followed by a complete uptake. abstract: Insulator-based electrokinetic (iEK) platforms integrate insulating structures within microchannels to amplify nonlinear electrophoresis (EPNL) effects and improve separation efficiency, as such effects scale with the electric field magnitude and introduce more discriminatory characteristics. In contrast, free solution platforms, used in conventional capillary electrophoresis (CE) systems, traditionally neglect EPNL effects and rely on the electrical charge of target analytes alone to perform separations by employing linear electrophoresis (EPL). In this work, the effects of EPNL in free solution platforms are tested by separating a binary mixture of microparticles and a charge-identical binary mixture of microparticles and Bacillus cereus cells. title: Morphology-Controlled Transition between Interfacial Slip and Drag over a Pinned Surface Nanobubble under Electrowetting-Inspired Control
abstract: Surface nanobubbles are known to influence interfacial slip and near-wall hydrodynamics, yet the role of actively controlled nanobubble morphology in regulating momentum transfer at solid-liquid interfaces remains insufficiently understood. Here, nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations are used to investigate a pinned surface nanobubble located at a wettability step in a confined water nanochannel. An electrowetting-inspired interfacial forcing (Fext) is applied near the solid surface to tune the effective solid-liquid wettability, thereby inducing reversible deformation of the pinned nanobubble from a flattened configuration to a more protruding morphology. title: Computer-Assisted Workflow for DNA Origami-Engineered Triangular Nanopores
abstract: Synthetic nanopores engineered by DNA origami provide a highly biocompatible and structurally programmable platform for elucidating the transmembrane mechanisms of functional macromolecules. However, engineering large DNA nanopores exceeding 30 nm in width remains a significant challenge. Here, we introduce a computer-assisted workflow to significantly reduce the design time and characterization costs of 45 nm-wide triangular DNA nanopores compared to empirical approaches. By leveraging extensive computational simulations, the feasibility of the triangular nanopore design was first validated. title: Interfacial Coordination and Dimensional Confinement Enable Continuous Thin MOF-on-MOF Membranes for Ion Sieving
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with crystallographically defined pores and chemically programmable internal structures are attractive candidates for regulating ion transport at the molecular scale. Yet, it is still difficult to grow MOF-on-MOF structures as continuous thin membranes because the secondary phase usually forms either thick coatings or discontinuous particles, both of which hinder ion transport. In this work, we found that Cu-O-Zr coordination at the interface can guide UiO-66 to grow continuously on the CuOx-BDC scaffold even under severe lattice mismatch, producing a thin integrated membrane. title: Hydration Topology Manipulates CO2 Transport in Water-Saturated Micropores of Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract The confinement effect of nanochannels (<2 nm) dictates the gas–liquid distribution at solid–liquid interfaces, yet the effect of interfacial chemistry on their kinetic behaviors lacks insightful understanding. Particularly, the interfacial CO2 transport mechanism is critical for CO2 capture in hydrated environments. Herein, we employ nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations combined with density functional theory calculations to elucidate CO2 transport mechanisms in fully hydrated one-dimensional micropores of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). title: Electronic-Friction-Modulated Water Slip at MoS2-Based van der Waals Heterostructures–Water Interfaces
abstract: Friction is a key determinant governing energy dissipation at solid-water interfaces, but the interfacial friction mechanism remains poorly understood. Herein, we systematically investigated water slip in MoS2/(WS2, hBN, and graphene) van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) with MoS2 as the top layer. title: Hydrophobic Confinement Enables Direct Identification of Thyroid Hormones with Single-Atom Resolution
abstract: The direct detection of small hydrophobic biomolecules remains a major challenge for biological nanopores. This is due to the weak interactions provided by the hydrophilic lumens, which result in ultrafast translocation and insufficient molecular recognition. Here, to reconcile the hydrophilicity for ionic flow and hydrophobic interactions for molecule recognition, we engineer a hydrophobic confinement stabilized by an interconnected hydrogen-bond network. title: Reconfigurable Magnetic Nanopore Platform for Selective Trapping
abstract: Solid-state nanopores offer a powerful platform for nanoscale analysis of individual analytes, including biomolecules and functionalized nanoparticles, by confining them within a precisely defined sensing region. However, their inherently passive operation restricts practical applications, as they cannot precisely control particle position or dynamics inside the pore. Here, we introduce magnetic nanopore architectures that integrate a ferromagnetic layer into the nanopore system. Acting as a magnetic discontinuity within an otherwise uniformly magnetized film, the nanopore generates localized stray magnetic fields that enable magnetic tweezing of magnetic nanoparticles, which can be functionalized with fluorescent biomolecules. title: Interfacial Synthesis of Two‐Dimensional Network Membranes for Osmotic Energy Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) network‐structured materials, encompassing 2D polymers and covalent organic frameworks, have captivated researchers with their highly ordered, porous architectures that promote efficient mass transport and versatile functionalities across diverse applications. However, fabricating crystalline 2D network membranes with precise functionalization and ultrathin profiles remains a persistent challenge, often limited by defect formation or scalability issues. Herein, we introduce a novel interfacial strategy employing photo‐triggered [2 + 2] cycloaddition at the air/water interface to synthesize ultrathin (∼1.5 nm), crystalline 2D network membranes from styrylpyridine‐armed monomers. title: Multifactorial Regulation Mechanisms of Negative Differential Resistance in Macropores
abstract: The negative differential resistance (NDR) effect provides nonlinear control over ionic current and has important potential in ion sensing and information storage. A multiphys-ics numerical model is established using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.3, coupling the Poisson−Nernst−Planck and Navier−Stokes equations to investigate the effects of solution concentration gradient, pore length, pore diameter, and surface charge density on NDR effect. title: Tuning cross-stream lift in viscoelastic shear: Distinct hydrodynamic signatures of force-bearing and force-free mechanisms
abstract: We investigate the lift and drag corrections acting on a particle suspended in a planar viscoelastic shear flow when the particle is tuned to translate relative to the flow by an external mechanism. title: Inferring surface slip in active colloids from flow fields using physics-informed neural networks
abstract: The directed motion of active colloids is governed by spatial variations in surface chemistry that generate effective interfacial flows, yet the resulting slip distributions remain extremely difficult to measure directly. title: Electrostatic and hydrodynamic modulation of resistive pulse waveforms for nanoparticle sensing
abstract: Recently, detection and filtering techniques of nanoobjects have attracted significant attention. title: Physical–Chemical Cross-Linked Amphoteric Ion-Exchange Membranes for Energy-Efficient Acid–Alkaline Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Acid–alkaline amphoteric water electrolysis is highly promising for energy-efficient hydrogen production, yet navigating the trade-off between membrane conductivity and long-term stability remains challenging. title: Chemically Gated Reconfigurable Nanofluidic Synapse Enables Metaplasticity and Neuromorphic Sound Recognition
abstract: Metaplasticity, the adaptive regulation of synaptic plasticity, is fundamental to biological information processing but remains challenging to implement in artificial systems, especially in fluidic environments. Herein, we address this challenge by developing a graphene oxide-based nanofluidic synapse capable of reconfigurable plasticity, where synaptic plasticity can be reversibly regulated via extrinsic ionic cues. abstract: Relative to liquid chromatography coupled to electrospray ionization (ESI), paper spray ionization (PSI) can more rapidly ionize analytes from complex matrices with less sample preparation and less expensive instrumentation. title: Decoupling Diffusion- and Field-Driven Ion Transport in Graphene Oxide/Tungsten Disulfide Heterolaminar Composites
abstract: Laminar graphene oxide (GO) films provide a model platform for studying ion transport in nanometer-scale two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels. title: Kinetic–Thermodynamic Coupling for Enhanced Water Isotopologue Separation Via Solar-Powered Diffusion–Evaporation
abstract: Separating water isotopologues is highly energy-intensive because the nearly identical physicochemical properties of H2O and D2O impose intrinsically small thermodynamic differences, limiting the efficiency of conventional thermal separation processes. Here, we report a solar-powered diffusion-evaporation coupling (SDEC) strategy that integrates nonequilibrium transport with interfacial phase transition to enable efficient H2O/D2O separation. abstract: Abstract A microchannel reactor is believed to be effective equipment to implement electrosynthesis for its short distance between electrodes to reduce the energy cost of ion transport in electrolytic solutions. title: PFAS-induced modulation of vesicle diffusiophoresis
abstract: Understanding how per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) partition into biological membranes and alter their properties is central for elucidating PFAS toxicity. title: Brinkman Electro-Osmotic Crossflow in a Microtube with a Hydrophobic and Randomly Corrugated Wall
abstract: A second-order domain perturbation analysis is developed for electro-osmotic transport through a long, rigid microtube containing a Newtonian electrolyte and a homogeneous porous matrix. title: Salinity-Dependent PFOA Transport and Membrane Stability in a Hybrid Electrokinetic–Ion Exchange System for Produced Water
abstract: Abstract Produced water is a challenging industrial wastewater because its high salinity and complex ionic composition can strongly influence electrically driven contaminant transport and membrane stability. This study investigated a two-stage hybrid electrokinetic–ion exchange membrane (EK–IEM) process for PFOA removal from produced water, focusing on the coupled effects of salinity, ionic transport, electrical loading, energy demand, and membrane stability. abstract: Abstract The present work investigates the electroosmotic peristaltic transport of a Bingham fluid through an inclined microchannel, considering variable fluid properties and compliant channel walls. title: Selective Monovalent Cation Transport in Two‐Dimensional Polymer Membranes via Charge Control of Nanochannels
abstract: ABSTRACT Monovalent cations like Li + , Na + , and K + are now regarded as important components for advanced electrochemical energy storage technologies for achieving high energy density and power density. title: Two-Dimensional Membranes for High-Value Ion Separation from Seawater and Brines
abstract: Seawater and brines contain substantial inventories of high-value ions, yet their extraction is constrained by dilute targets, concentrated competitors and feed-dependent speciation. title: Measuring Blood Plasma Glutamine Levels Using a Nanopore‐Based Sensor
abstract: Measuring blood glutamine (GLN) levels is valuable for managing urea cycle disorders. Currently, patients visit the hospital to have their GLN levels checked using analytical techniques that, despite being highly accurate and reliable, lead to long waiting times and delay clinical decisions. A point-of-care device would enable patients to monitor GLN levels at home, allowing for greater control over the condition. Here, we made use of a highly sensitive GLN biosensor system based on dodecameric Cytolysin A variant AS (ClyA-AS) nanopore coupled with the GLN-specific protein, the substrate-binding domain 2 (SBD2). Measurements are performed on a single ClyA-AS nanopore embedded into an artificial lipid bilayer, where the application of a small voltage generates ionic currents that report on the binding and unbinding of GLN (added in the trans side of ClyA-AS) to SBD2 (added in cis). We dem
reason: Demonstrates nanopore-based biosensor for point-of-care glutamine monitoring in blood plasma.

title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
abstract: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model. By representing membrane chemical potential barriers and active pump potentials via smoothed Eulerian kernels ($Ψ_w, \mathcal{H}_w$), we formulate the passive dynamics as an $L^2$-Wasserstein ($W_2$) gradient flow coupled to non-conservative active pushing fields representing ATP-driven $3:2$ $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ exchangers. We establish global weak existence of solutions to the continuous Poisson--Nernst--Planck--IB system via a split-step Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational scheme, backed by Calderón--Zygmund bounds for non-local Poisson drift and $H^3(\mathbb{S}^1)$ interface regularity under Stokes flow. title: Co-ion-dependent ion sorption and diffusion in graphene oxide membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphene oxide membranes (GOMs) are promising materials for ion separation in energy, water, and environmental applications. However, quantitative understanding of how co-ion identity, concentration and ion association govern sorption and transport in GO nanochannels remains limited. Here, we combine equilibrium sorption measurements with concentration-gradient and electric-field-driven transport experiments to quantify individual ion diffusion coefficients in GOMs equilibrated with Na 2 SO 4 , MgSO 4 , and NaNO 3 and benchmark the results against chloride electrolytes. The results show that Mg 2+ uptake in MgSO 4 solutions is lower than in MgCl 2. In both magnesium- and sodium-based systems, the sulfate concentrations are lower than that of the corresponding monovalent co-ions. reason: Quantifies co-ion-dependent ion sorption and diffusion in graphene oxide nanochannels, relevant to electrokinetic transport.

title: Controlled Competition Reduces Errors in Nanostructure-Based DNA Data Storage
abstract: DNA nanotechnology offers a promising route toward molecular data storage with exceptional density, longevity, and energy efficiency. Unlike sequence-based approaches that rely on large-scale synthesis and sequencing, structural DNA data storage encodes information into spatial architectures readable at the single-molecule level. However, practical implementation is hindered by substitution errors -particularly 0-to-1 “bit flips” - that arise during pooled readout and compromise data fidelity. Here, we introduce and systematically benchmark a set of thermodynamically-tuned error protection strategies for DNA ‘hard drive’ nanostructures, based on controlled competition between a label strand and a protector strand. reason: Develops error protection for DNA nanostructure data storage readout via solid-state nanopore sensing.

title: Chitosan‐Gated Polycarbonate Nanochannels for Tunable Water and Cation Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological membranes regulate transport by responding to pH changes and ion binding. Emulating this logic, chitosan is introduced into cylindrical nanochannels of multiporous polycarbonate ion‐track‐etched membranes via covalent immobilization or electrostatic adsorption. Chitosan is confined within the nanochannels, leaving outer‐surface liquid–solid interactions unchanged. The channels remain open when dry, while upon hydration the polymer swells and modulates water and ion transport. Chitosan shifts the membrane from microfiltration to ultrafiltration via swelling‐driven steric hindrance. Consistent with reduced water flux, the flux of tris(2,2′‐bipyridine)ruthenium(II) (Ru(bpy) 3 2 + ) decreases by ∼75% and ∼92% at pH 7.5 and pH 2.5, respectively, compared to pristine nanochannels. reason: Demonstrates pH/ion-responsive nanochannels for tunable water and cation transport, relevant to biomimetic ion transport control.

title: Selective Interfacial Regulation of LiMn 2 O 4 for Flow Electrochemical Lithium Extraction
abstract: ABSTRACT Gas‐produced water (GPW) is increasingly recognized as an important low‐quality aqueous lithium resource. Electrochemical lithium extraction using LiMn 2 O 4 (LMO) offers a promising strategy for lithium extraction from aqueous resources. However, its application to GPW is hindered by competing‐ion co‐intercalation and Mn dissolution, which compromise extraction selectivity and stability. Inspired by selective ion transport in biological ion pumps, a Li 0.33 La 0.56 TiO 3 (LLTO)‐engineered LMO interface is developed to integrate Li + ‐sieving nanochannels with interfacial stabilization. Experimental and mechanistic analyses demonstrate that the LLTO‐engineered interface promotes local Li + enrichment, while its Li + ‐sieving nanochannels restrict competing‐cation access, thereby accelerating selective Li + transport and optimizing Li + storage. reason: Develops Li+-selective nanochannels in LLTO-coated LMO for electrochemical lithium extraction from brine.

title: A57-4 Hypothesis of Nanoscale Arch Self-Locking of Water Molecules | 水分子纳米拱自锁理论(原创推演版)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This work originates from introspective observation of ancient water conservancy projects and a fundamental inquiry into the nature of fluid pressure. The conventional intuition holds that a hydraulic head difference inevitably drives fluid flow. However, pressure arises from extrusion transmission rather than elevation itself. Without confining boundaries to sustain extrusion, gravitational potential dissipates and cannot build up pressure matching the elevation difference. From this, a counterintuitive conjecture emerges: sufficiently strong extrusion may amplify structural constraints and induce jamming. A macroscopic thought experiment using equal-diameter spherical particles (soybean arch) is constructed, and its isomorphic logic is transferred to the nanoscale. title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
abstract: Nanofluidic memristors promise brain-inspired information processing with ions, yet their microscopic origin remains debated. So far, ionic memory has been attributed to ion-specific interactions, dynamic wetting, chemical reactions or mechanical deformations, yet typically without direct experimental evidence. Here, by combining operando interferometric imaging with electrokinetic measurements, we directly visualize voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels as the key origin of memristive hysteresis. We identify two distinct classes of blisters: unidirectional, driven by electrostatic forces on surface charges, and bidirectional, arising from osmotic pressure due to concentration polarization. reason: Direct imaging reveals voltage-induced blistering as mechanism for ionic memory in 2D nanochannels.

title: An Analytical Pore-Scale Model for Predicting Permeability from Electrical Conductivity
abstract: Electrical signals carry the fingerprints of subsurface hydraulic behavior, yet the methods used to interpret them remain fragile. For example, the Archie–Kozeny–Carman approach, long standard in hydrogeophysics and petrophysics, rely on empirical and oversimplified assumptions of pore geometry homogeneity and isotropy. In reality, the subsurface comprises stratified layers, fractures, and conduits where these assumptions fail, yielding permeability estimates that are uncertain, locally biased, and insensitive to the true complexity of fluid pathways.,Here, we present three interlinked advances that reframe permeability prediction from electrical measurements. reason: Develops electrokinetic pore-scale model linking electrical conductivity to permeability.

title: A Portable UV-LED Dual-Nafion Microfluidic Platform for Label-Free Trace Protein Preconcentration and Absorbance Detection
abstract: Sensitive label-free detection of low-abundance proteins requires both effective on-chip preconcentration and a compact, low-noise optical readout for use outside conventional laboratories. Here, we present a portable UV-LED dual-Nafion microfluidic platform that integrates a 280 nm UV-LED, a chromium-coated slot collimator, a dual-Nafion ion concentration polarization (ICP) preconcentrator, and a miniature spectrometer within a 3D-printed enclosure. The symmetric dual-Nafion geometry on a UV-transparent quartz substrate confines the ICP enrichment zone to a fixed 120 × 500 µm interrogation window, enabling spatially stable, label-free on-chip absorbance monitoring at 280 nm. title: Dramatic pressure-induced slowdown and the soft glassy rheology of water at 2D material interface
abstract: The flow of molecularly confined water has attracted considerable interest in recent years. Yet despite their exquisite character, current nanofluidic devices cannot probe molecular water flow beyond the linear-response regime, while nanomechanical force- based approaches have produced markedly inconsistent results. Here, using tuning- fork-based atomic force microscopy, we tackle these limitations by measuring the full linear-to-nonlinear, shear-dependent viscoelastic rheology of molecularly confined water at various two-dimensional material interfaces -- demonstrating pronounced rate effects in water flow response. title: Electrohydraulic fields generated by active transport at tissue interfaces
abstract: Living cells and tissues can generate complex patterns of electric fields and fluid flows which can play important role in physiology. Both, fields and flows are rooted in ion transport across biological interfaces: cell membranes and epithelial cell layers. Here we develop a unified electrohydraulic framework that combines electric fields, osmotic pressures, and fluid flows, emphasising their couplings. We show that spatially heterogeneous ion transport acts as a distributed current source, generating long-range electric fields, osmotic gradients, and fluid flows. title: pH-Driven Restructuring of Hydration Layers and Cation Adsorption at the Alumina–Water Interface
abstract: Oxide–water interfaces underpin ion separations, catalysis, and electrochemical energy technologies, where the electrical double layer (EDL) controls adsorption, transport, and reactivity. title: High-Frequency Mass Transfer Enabling Over-Limiting Currents in Porous Electrodes
abstract: Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. However, over-limiting currents (OLCs), which exceed this limit, are often observed and have been attributed to surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic effects. title: Fabrication and evaluation of self-aligned funnel inlets for DNA analysis in nanochannels
abstract: A variety of DNA analysis techniques are enabled by linearization of the macromolecules through physical confinement in nanochannels. This work demonstrates the first nanolithography-free method for creating funneled inlets for nanochannels that are themselves fabricated without nanolithography. A self-aligning, anisotropic funnel etch step was introduced, which widens the entrance of the nanochannel by a factor of 10. Additionally, the shape of the funnel can be controlled by the etch parameters from an 8° inlet angle to 34°. Funneled inlets are suitable to reduce the entropic barrier and increase the amount of DNA molecules introduced into a nanochannel. title: Impedance of an electric double layer capacitor with a multi-component electrolyte
abstract: I derive the impedance response of an ideal electrolyte containing an arbitrary number of mobile ionic species between blocking planar electrodes, described by the Poisson--Nernst--Planck equations. title: Electrolyte and Voltage Operating Window for Reversible Plasmid Capture
abstract: Abstract Electro-modulated separation enables ligand-free capture and release of charged biomolecules through electrically controlled interactions with conductive surfaces. This study defined the operating window for reversible capture of the model plasmid pVAX1 on non-functionalized pencil graphite electrodes by evaluating applied cell voltage, initial plasmid concentration, buffer composition, electrolyte conditions, and plasmid stability. title: Steady translation of a chemically active viscous drop along a rigid wall
abstract: Chemically active drops release a chemical solute, gradients in whose concentration cause interfacial flows that advect the emitted solute. This non-linear coupling between solute distribution and fluid flow causes the drop to swim via an advective instability, if the system's Peclet number Pe--ratio of advective-to-diffusive solute transport--is larger than a finite threshold. title: Membrane-driven and hybrid pathways for magnesium recovery from aqueous brines and industrial wastewater: a review
abstract: Magnesium is a critical raw material with growing industrial demand, yet vast and largely untapped reservoirs exist in desalination reject brines, saltwork bitterns, hypersaline lake brines, and industrial wastewaters. Magnesium recovery from these streams is attracting increasing attention as a strategy to reduce brine disposal, mitigate salinity-management challenges, and decrease reliance on energy-intensive primary production. This review critically evaluates membrane-based and membrane-enabled hybrid routes for magnesium recovery, with conventional methods introduced briefly as a performance baseline. title: Graphitic Carbon Nitride‐Based Microrobots: Progress and Prospects in Environmental and Biomedical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphitic carbon nitride (g‐C 3 N 4 ) is a metal‐free semiconductor responsive to visible light that has attracted considerable interest as a photocatalyst in environmental and biomedical applications. Constructing photocatalysts as light‐driven microrobots allows simultaneous propulsion and catalytic activity, both driven by photoinduced charge separation. In addition, light‐driven systems can perform remote control of micro/nanorobots (MNRs) and reduce their reliance on external chemical fuels. Thus, g‐C 3 N 4 has been investigated as a functional material for microrobots, owing to its low cost, chemical stability, and biocompatibility. abstract: This study presents an analytical investigation of electroosmotic magnetohydrodynamic (EMHD) mixed convection flow of nanofluids in a vertical microchannel, with emphasis on the coupled transport mechanisms relevant to microscale electrokinetic and thermal-management systems. abstract: ABSTRACT Electrokinetically powered peristaltic transport has been gaining substantial attention due to its potential applications in the areas of biomedical engineering, smart microfluidic devices, controlled drug delivery, and compact cooling techniques. abstract: We present a novel mechanism for the emergence of non-reciprocal interactions in a single-species suspension of chemically active colloids made out of semi-permeable vesicles, which encapsulate enzymes that catalyze a non-linear chemical reaction. title: Advances and future perspectives on electrodialysis for sustainable critical raw material refining
abstract: Critical raw materials (CRM) are important for electrification, renewable energy and the transition toward a circular economy. Conventional extraction and refining methods are often associated with high chemical consumption, complex process flowsheets and significant residue formation. Electrodialysis has emerged as a promising tool to reduce chemical consumption and lower residue production. The technique relies on an electric field to transfer ions across an arrangement of ion-exchange membranes and has long been used in desalination applications. abstract: Isolating radionuclides is a critical challenge in the geological disposal of high-level radioactive waste. abstract: ABSTRACT Natural scallion membranes located on the inner wall leaf sheaths serve as inherent nanofluidic channels for the transport of soluble nutrients and ions during plant growth, thus providing a promising candidate for fabricating low‐cost, sustainable, and high‐performance ion‐selective nanofluidic membranes toward osmotic power generation. abstract: Many problems in soft matter research involve particles suspended in a solvent, where hydrodynamic interactions play a crucial role. abstract: It is a well-known principle that like charges repel, whether positive or negative. However, experiments on electrically charged matter suspended in liquids have frequently reported the opposite: attraction between like-charged particles, rather than repulsion. Experiments have also shown that the sign of the force at large separations can depend on the sign of the particle charge, e.g., in water negative particles attract, while positives repel as expected, and this trend generally reverses in polar organic solvents such as alcohols. These observations cannot be reconciled with standing theories of the electrostatic interaction that regard the intervening solvent medium as a structureless, featureless dielectric continuum. Recent work has called for the traditional continuum view of the medium to be relinquished, attributing the observed attraction to an "electrosolvation force" - a ter
reason: Discusses electrosolvation forces and like-charged attraction, fundamental to electrokinetic interactions in solvents.

title: Confinement-induced transitions in the dynamics of self-diffusiophoretic microswimmer under Poiseuille flow
abstract: The dynamics of artificial microswimmers in confined flows remain poorly understood despite their relevance to microfluidics, drug delivery, and the navigation of active particles through physiological pathways. Here, we investigate the self-diffusiophoretic motion of spherical Janus particles in pressure-driven Poiseuille flow within microchannels, systematically spanning the weak to strong confinement regime. Using bispherical eigenfunction expansions for the solute and flow fields, we analyze swimmer-boundary interactions in weak to moderate confinement, while complementary finite-element simulations are employed to examine the strongly confined regime without invoking artificial steric potentials. reason: Examines confinement effects on diffusiophoretic microswimmers in Poiseuille flow, revealing trajectory transitions.

title: Non-contact dielectrophoretic forcing of particle-laden flow: Momentum transfer and flow modulation in a blood-mimicking suspension
abstract: Dielectrophoresis (DEP) provides a non-contact forcing mechanism for polarizable particles suspended in non-uniform electric fields. While DEP is commonly used for particle manipulation, trapping, and separation, its role as a distributed hydrodynamic forcing mechanism in particle-laden suspension flow remains less explored. This study investigates DEP-assisted flow modulation in a diluted glycerol–SiO2 suspension used as a controllable blood-mimicking particle-laden phantom. The fracture-healing context provides the transport motivation, whereas the central focus is the particle–fluid momentum-transfer mechanism. Three external coil geometries, Catenary, Lintearia, and Valeria, were evaluated at excitation currents of 0.50, 0.75, and 1.00 A, respectively. reason: Dielectrophoretic forcing modulates flow in blood-mimicking suspension, demonstrating electrokinetic momentum transfer for biomedical applications.

title: An Electrochemiluminescence Biosensing Platform Based on a Hydrogel-AAO Nanochannel Membrane for GFAP Detection
abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors are widely used for ultrasensitive bioanalysis; however, their practical application is often limited by insufficient interface stability under complex detection conditions. Herein, an integrated hydrogel-AAO membrane (HAM) as a novel composite ion-exchange membrane is developed for constructing stable ECL biosensing interfaces. In the HAM architecture, the agarose hydrogel provides a three-dimensional, biocompatible matrix for antibody immobilization and target recognition, while the highly ordered AAO nanochannels serve as an efficient ion-transport and signal transduction pathway. The composite membrane enables effective coupling between interfacial biorecognition events and ECL signal modulation while physically separating the recognition layer from the ECL reaction region. Using glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), a clinically relevant b
reason: Integrates nanochannels in a composite membrane for stable electrochemiluminescence biosensing of biomarkers.

title: Fabrication of MoS2 Nanopores via Dielectric Breakdown for Single-Molecule Sensing Applications
abstract: This study focuses on the controllable fabrication of monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) nanopores based on dielectric breakdown and their application in single-molecule sensing. To address the poor pore-size controllability and limited reproducibility commonly encountered in the fabrication of sub-5 nm transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanopores, the nanopore formation processes under voltage-stepping and current-stepping modes were systematically investigated. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the voltage-stepping mode, the current-stepping mode exhibits a more gradual breakdown transition. Although the average breakdown times of the two modes are comparable, the nanopores fabricated by current stepping are confined to a narrower sub-5 nm range, whereas voltage stepping produces a broader distribution. reason: Presents controlled fabrication of MoS2 nanopores for single-molecule DNA sensing applications.

title: Solvent dependency of the free energy landscape of a protein translocating graphene nanopores
abstract: The translocation of (bio)polymers through nanometer-sized openings in solid-state materials is a key process that allows us to identify the identity, length, and sequence of the biopolymer. The efficiency and speed of this process, however, are influenced by the local environment and the interatomic interactions among all components: the biopolymer, pore material, and solvent environment. In order to quantify and understand this influence, we perform all-atom molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling, implementing metadynamics. For this, we use a model biomolecule, part of the H4 histone protein, and a two-dimensional graphene nanopore. To assess the translocation process and the underlying free-energy landscape of the protein, we model the process within a simple monovalent solution, as well as in a molecular denaturant. reason: Studies protein translocation free-energy landscapes in graphene nanopores, relevant to nanopore sensing physics.

title: Gradient‐Oxidized Bacterial Cellulose for Self‐Sustained Soil Moisture Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil moisture monitoring is pivotal to precision agricultural irrigation. Conventional soil moisture sensors rely on external power supplies and suffer from poor environmental compatibility. The facile fabrication of hydrovoltaic devices with asymmetric film structures remains challenging, and related designs tailored for soil scenarios are still insufficient. Here, we report an in situ‐grown planar asymmetric encapsulated bacterial cellulose (AEBC) device for self‐powered soil moisture sensing. Graphene oxide (GO) and carbon nanotubes (CNT) are sequentially embedded on opposite sides of the growing cellulose network via gravity‐assisted in situ assembly, forming an oxygen‐functional gradient. reason: Asymmetric hydrovoltaic bacterial cellulose device for self-powered moisture sensing, relevant to electrokinetic energy harvesting.

title: Single-Cell Capture and Electrically Induced In-Plane Rotation with Frequency-Dependent Spatial Segregation Using Serrated Floating Electrodes
abstract: Abstract Precise single-cell manipulation is essential for investigating cellular heterogeneity and enabling downstream bioanalytical applications. However, conventional dielectrophoretic platforms often suffer from excessive field localization, multi-cellular aggregation, and complicated electrode integration, limiting their controllability and scalability. Here, we present a microfluidic platform based on serrated floating electrodes for multimodal single-cell manipulation through frequency-dependent electrokinetic regulation. Periodically arranged driving and floating electrodes generate spatially confined high-gradient electric fields that enable deterministic single-cell trapping under low-voltage excitation. reason: Enables single-cell trapping and rotation via frequency-dependent dielectrophoresis on serrated floating electrodes.

title: Dielectrophoretic and Thermophoretic Control of Particles with Laser-Illuminated Electrode Arrays Embedded in Microfluidic Channels
abstract: Abstract Metal electrodes integrated into microfluidic channels are used to manipulate particles through a combination of dielectrophoretic and thermophoretic forces. The electrode arrays are milled into a thin metal film disposed in a microfluidic channel to precisely position the arrays within the fluid flow. Upon laser illumination, these electrode arrays exert forces on nearby particles that are coupled with microfluidic flow. The primary modes of particle-electrode interactions are lateral attraction, particle capture, edge confinement, and particle repulsion. reason: Combines dielectrophoretic and thermophoretic forces for particle control in microfluidics, demonstrating coupled electro-thermal transport.

abstract: Since Taylor’s seminal work on the dispersion of soluble matter, the modelling and control of solute dispersion have received considerable attention. This study investigates the solute dispersion in polymer solutions driven by unsteady magnetohydrodynamic (MHD)-oscillatory electro-osmotic flow within a microtube, aiming to reveal the transport mechanisms in complex rheological media through microscale flow. Firstly, based on the Debye–Hückel approximation, analytical solutions for the electric potential and velocity distributions of mixed MHD-electrohydrodynamic flows are rigorously derived. Subsequently, using Sankarasubramanian & Gill’s generalised dispersion model (1970 Proc. R. Soc. Lond. title: Nanopipette Sensing of APE1 Activity via Enzymatic Recycling and DNA Tetrahedron−Streptavidin Reporting: Profiling in Cancer Diagnostics, Oxidative Stress, and Cell Cycle
abstract: Abstract Apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) is a clinical biomarker whose small molecular size hinders direct detection by conventional nanopores (30 nm). Here, we report a nanopipette platform integrating APE1-driven enzymatic recycling amplification with DNA tetrahedron−streptavidin (TDN−SA) complex-based resistive-pulse reporting to overcome this size limitation. APE1 specifically cleaves hairpin DNA probes, generating output strands that displace biotin-modified DNA oligo from the TDN−SA complex, reducing translocation event frequency in 30 nm nanopipettes. This signal modulation enables APE1 quantification with a detection limit of 10−5 U/mL and a linear range spanning 7 orders of magnitude (10−5 to 10 U/mL). reason: Nanopipette resistive-pulse sensing with enzymatic amplification for protein detection, advancing nanopore sensing methodology.

title: Chiral Solid-State Nanopores Amplify Secondary Interactions for Ionic-Current Discrimination of Neurotransmitter Enantiomers
abstract: Abstract Single-molecule ionic-current sensing provides a powerful electroanalytical route for resolving small-molecule enantiomers, yet reliable discrimination remains difficult when stereochemical differences generate only weak and transient interfacial interactions. Here, we engineer a chiral solid-state nanopore by integrating an ultrathin β-cyclodextrin/trimesoyl chloride (β-CD/TMC) nanomembrane onto TiO2 nanopores and confining l-tryptophan within the interfacial host−guest microenvironment. The resulting chiral interface amplifies secondary noncovalent interactions under nanoscale confinement and converts subtle stereochemical asymmetry into distinguishable ionic-current blockade signatures. reason: Engineers chiral β-CD/TMC nanopores to discriminate neurotransmitter enantiomers via amplified ionic-current signatures.

title: Biased active particles in a three-dimensional tube: Theory, simulations, and validity criterion
abstract: We investigate the biased transport of active Brownian particles (ABPs) confined in a three-dimensional (3D) corrugated tube under a constant external bias. Within a sufficiently low-activity regime, we derive a generalized Fick-Jacobs (FJ) equation that reduces the 3D Fokker-Planck equation to an effective one-dimensional (1D) equation under the assumption that particles quickly reach a steady state along the transverse directions of the tube. The transport characteristics of ABPs are computed semi-analytically using the FJ approximation and corroborated by numerical simulation results of the 3D tube. reason: Derives generalized Fick-Jacobs equation for biased active particle transport in 3D corrugated tubes, relevant to confined diffusio-kinetic transport.

abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐asymmetric pacman shaped colloids generate motion through degradation of . In simulation, using ; the phoretic mobility of the particle, ; the production rate of the particle and , the initial angle of the particle, these Pacman particles orientate their bodies according to self‐generated fluid flows. Furthermore, the ability of Pacman particles to respond to chemical and light stimuli is studied in experiments. title: Machine Learning-Assisted Discrimination of Isobaric Histone Acetylations by Nanopore
abstract: Histone acetylation, a post-translational modification, is associated with cancer progression, invasion, and metastasis, serving as a promising biomarker. The accurate discrimination of acetylation sites has strong potential for cancer diagnostics. Herein, we engineered an R220Q aerolysin nanopore to detect isobaric histone acetylations. By exposing the paired negative charge (D222) at the pore entrance, peptides with a higher positive charge density encounter a lower U* for pore entry and subsequent translocation. With the assistance of machine learning, we achieved direct discrimination of isobaric acetylations in histone peptides. Monoacetylated peptides H3K9ac and H3K14ac, as well as diacetylated peptides H3K4acK9ac and H3K4acK14ac were unambiguously identified in mixtures with identification accuracies of 99.4% and 98.8%, respectively. title: Controlled Ion Dehydration-Driven Catalysis Enabled by Reverse-Mode Nanofiltration
abstract: Catalysis under nanoscale confinement is widely pursued, but practical systems remain limited by a persistent contradiction: maximizing confinement-enhanced reactivity usually increases the residence time and accelerates pore failure. Here we present a ceramic nanofiltration platform that resolves this trade-off by coupling subnanometer confinement with transient, flow-through ion dehydration. The membrane is constructed by atomic layer deposition on a hierarchical α-Al2O3/γ-Al2O3 scaffold, yielding a robust, ultrathin Al2O3 active layer with tunable nanochannels and minimized transport distance to the reaction interface. reason: Studies ion dehydration in subnanometer channels during nanofiltration, relevant to confined ion transport mechanisms.

title: Leveraging Electroosmosis in OmpF for Robust Peptide Sensing
abstract: Peptide sensing and sequencing are essential for elucidating sequence-function relationships and evaluating the peptide drug quality. Nanopore electrochemistry enables label-free characterization of peptide composition, structure, and interactions at the single-molecule level through ionic-current fingerprints. However, efficient capture remains challenging for low-abundance peptides with heterogeneous charge and conformational properties. Herein, we study peptide capture by the asymmetric OmpF nanopore and examine the relative contributions of electroosmotic flow (EOF), electrophoretic force (EPF), peptide conformation, and field-gradient-mediated interactions. The laterally heterogeneous charge distribution within OmpF modulates the salt dependence of ionic screening and electroosmotic transport, supporting an efficient EOF-associated peptide capture under high-salt conditions. title: High Spatiotemporal Profiling of MiRNA and ROS Trafficking at Single Mitochondria with Functionalized θ-Nanopipette
abstract: The dysregulation of mitochondrial microRNA-125b (miR-125b) and overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS) are tightly implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the dynamic interplay between mitochondrial miR-125b and ROS, as well as their mutual regulatory mechanisms, remains poorly understood. Herein, we develop a functionalized θ-nanopipette integrated with two independent detection channels, which enables simultaneous, crosstalk-free determination of miR-125b and ROS at the subcellular level. reason: Develops θ-nanopipette for simultaneous miRNA/ROS detection in single mitochondria, demonstrating nanochannel electrochemical sensing for biomedical applications.

title: Characterization of Single Ribosomes and Virus Particles with Large-Diameter Perfringolysin O Nanopores
abstract: Abstract Existing biological nanopores are often too narrow to accommodate large proteins and biomolecular complexes in their native folded states, precluding the analysis of megadalton assemblies. Here, we report the self-assembly of the cholesterol-dependent cytolysin Perfringolysin O (PFO) into stable transmembrane nanopores composed of 46 ± 9 monomers, with an inner pore diameter of 28.5 ± 5.6 nm and a length of 9.8 nm. We demonstrate that despite the large size of the pore assembly, PFO pores exhibit a stable open-pore current with a high signal-to-noise ratio, making them suitable for resistive-pulse recordings. title: Kinetically Arrested Interfacial Polyelectrolyte Complexes Enable Ionic Rectification in Ionoelastomer Heterojunctions
abstract: At interfaces between oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, ionic double layers (IDLs) emerge that are often treated as ionic counterparts of semiconductor depletion layers. Yet this analogy overlooks the molecular deformability of polymer-tethered charges. Here, we show that IDLs in soft ionoelastomer(IE) heterojunctions undergo interfacial complexation, resulting in the formation of a kinetically arrested polyelectrolyte complex (PEC) layer. Selective counterion-exchange staining with ionic fluorophores reveals a micron-scale unstained interfacial PEC region─far exceeding the depletion length predicted from thermodynamic considerations of IDLs. This exclusion arises from a kinetically frozen glassy PEC that suppresses counterion exchange with ionic fluorophores. reason: Ionic rectification via kinetically arrested polyelectrolyte complexes at soft heterojunctions, relevant to nanofluidic ion transport.

title: Electrokinetic Enrichment and Purification of Proteins and Anions from High-salt Samples on Liquid Plasticine-Based Open Chip
abstract: Microfluidic chips are promising for on-site analysis in medical diagnostics and food safety because they enable miniaturized, integrated sample processing. However, the analysis of complex, salt-rich matrices of biological and food samples remain challenging for conventional closed chips and electrokinetic pretreatment methods. Here, we developed an open, reconfigurable electrophoresis chip based on liquid plasticine, in which a moving neutralization reaction electrophoresis system (MNRES) was implemented for high-salt sample pretreatment. Liquid plasticine enabled facile construction of pump-free, valve-free, optically transparent, and cuttable open reservoirs and channels. title: Vertical Nanoconfinement Suppresses Lateral Diffusion for Super-Resolved Spatiotemporal Mapping of Nanocatalytic Dynamics
abstract: Mapping catalytic activity at the single-nanoparticle level is critical for the rational design of high-performance materials. However, current optical techniques are fundamentally limited by molecular diffusion blur. This physical decoupling of the luminescent signal from the catalytic site creates a "spatial information gap" that post-processing alone cannot reconcile. Here, we report a super-resolved imaging platform that overcomes this limitation by utilizing the nanoconfinement effect within a Vertically Oriented Silica Mesoporous Film (VSMF). By confining light-emitting species within vertical nanochannels, we effectively suppress lateral diffusion and regulate mass transport. title: NAVIS: A LAMMPS-Python framework for efficient computation of nanochannel velocity and thermal interfacial slip
abstract: We present NAVIS ( NA nochannel V elocity and thermal I nterfacial S lip), a LAMMPS-Python scripted toolkit for computing the Navier (hydrodynamic) friction coefficient and Kapitza (thermal) resistance at arbitrary solid-fluid interfaces. NAVIS is based on equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) methods for calculating the linear response friction and thermal resistance at the interface, as well as the corresponding velocity and temperature slips. title: Thickness‐Gated Water and Electron Transport in Near‐Critical Ultrathin Polyethylene Membrane Electrodes
abstract: Electrochemical systems are constrained by a materials paradox: chemically robust porous separators are typically hydrophobic and electronically insulating, forcing bulky, carbon-rich interfaces to couple mass transport and electrical contact. Here we show that pushing freestanding porous polyethylene into a near-critical ultrathin regime turns thickness into a geometric gate, enabling these functions to be switched without chemical modification. title: Pressure-gated flexible nanofluidic memristor based on a probe-punctured PDMS membrane
abstract: A flexible nanofluidic memristor is demonstrated based on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) membrane containing a single nanopore formed by probe puncturing and controlled by external pressure. A PDMS prepolymer with a base-to-curing agent ratio of 10:1 is cast and cured into a thin, transferable film, which is then released and bonded onto a micromachined silicon window. A tungsten probe with an apex diameter of approximately 100 nm is employed to puncture the suspended membrane region under optical visualization. Following probe retraction, the viscoelastic membrane undergoes nearly complete self-closure, establishing a low-leakage baseline current ideal for pressure-gated ionic transport. title: Investigation of Multi-Ion Transport Properties in Cement Paste Based on a Multi-Scale Phase Evolution Model
abstract: Marine concrete structures are subjected to multiple aggressive ions that react with hydration products, driving dynamic phase evolution and altering ion transport pathways. This study develops a multi-scale lattice diffusion-reaction coupled framework grounded in a microstructural evolution model, incorporating a simplified analytical correction for the electrical double layer (EDL) effect. Validation against Poisson-Boltzmann numerical solutions across a pore size range of 1.5-50 nm confirms that the mean relative errors for monovalent, divalent, and trivalent ions remain within 10%. The phase evolution of cement paste under single-ion attack was simulated, and its impact on ion transport performance under multi-ion coupled ingress was systematically investigated. title: Numerical entropy analysis of MHD electro-osmotic flow of peristaltic movement in a nanofluid with a Darcy–Forchheimer porous medium
abstract: Abstract This study examines entropy generation in the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) electro-osmotic peristaltic flow of a nanofluid through an asymmetric microchannel saturated with a Darcy–Forchheimer porous medium, including Hall current, Joule heating, temperature-dependent thermal conductivity, and velocity and thermal slip. abstract: Thermal and mass transport mechanisms are essential, to targeted hyperthermia, and solute migration in electro-osmotically and cilia driven physiological flows. title: Non-equilibrium cyclic conformations of DNA under electrokinetic confinement
abstract: Classic nanofluidic devices harness geometric confinement to modulate single polymer conformation and control chain dynamics. While classic nanofluidic devices have given rise to a range of applications, they are fundamentally limited by the static nature of their construction, which restricts real time control over molecular conformations. The reversible electrokinetic confinement (RECON) technique enables time-dependent control of DNA conformations in nanowells via dynamic modulation of field-induced confinement. title: Long-time Brownian dynamics of hard and sticky colloids by geometric projection
abstract: Particle-resolved colloid simulations are often limited by the fastest microscopic time scale retained in the model, which can be many orders of magnitude shorter than the collective process of interest. This is especially restrictive for aggregating colloids, where explicit near-contact potentials force the time integration to resolve the rapid positional relaxation of bonded pairs within narrow attractive wells. title: Single-Molecule Microfluidics for Protein Analysis and Sensing
abstract: Single-molecule microfluidics has emerged as a powerful approach for protein analysis and sensing by combining ultrasensitive detection with precise fluid control at the micro- and nanoscale. In this review, we discuss recent advances in this area spanning continuous-flow detection, transport-based assays, matrix-assisted separations, and nanofluidic confinement. We also cover compartmentalization using droplet and digital microfluidics, together with microfluidics-enabled single-molecule fluorescence and super-resolution imaging. We highlight the quantitative molecular parameters accessible through these approaches, including absolute concentration, hydrodynamic radius, molecular mass, binding affinity and kinetic rate constants, conformational dynamics, molecular activity, and population heterogeneity. title: Phoretic interactions in two-medium wedge geometries
abstract: Abstract We investigate the diffusiophoretic motion of a chemically isotropic active colloid in a three-dimensional wedge formed by two distinct fluid media, in the limit of vanishing Péclet and Reynolds numbers. title: Advances in Fabrication and Biomedical Integration of Precision Electroporation Devices
abstract: Electroporation, a biophysical method that transiently permeabilizes cell membranes via externally applied electric pulses, has evolved from bulk, low-resolution approaches to highly controlled micro- and nano-electroporation (MEP/NEP) platforms. By inducing a transmembrane potential exceeding a critical threshold (≈0.5–1.5 V), nanoscale pores form, enabling delivery of nucleic acids, proteins, drugs, and probes without viral vectors or chemical carriers. Early work demonstrated efficient plasmid uptake in mouse lyoma cells using high-intensity, short-duration pulses, establishing the foundation for modern gene transfer applications. reason: Reviews advances in micro/nano-electroporation platforms for controlled biomedical cargo delivery.

title: Modeling of Metal Fiber-Enhanced Ion Transport in Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries employing a metal fiber fleece as a 3D current collector show an improved ion diffusivity in the electrolyte due to additional surface transport in the electrical double layer at the fiber surface. Since the metal fiber fleece is electrochemically inactive, the objective is to identify a fiber architecture where the enhanced diffusivity overcompensates for the inactive volume penalty. For optimization of the copper fiber architecture in a graphite half-cell, a reduced Poisson-Boltzmann model coupled with a surface diffusion mechanism is fitted against microfluidic channel experiments and integrated into a pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) battery model. reason: Modeling of surface diffusion in electrical double layer on metal fibers, relevant to electrokinetic ion transport.

abstract: Abstract High-order memristor is needed in neuromorphic engineering for sophisticated neural encoding. Progress has been made in solid-state memristor with electronic dynamics, which, however, presents a significant disparity with the ionic-chemical signaling in the human brain. reason: Realizes high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding via ion transport in confined covalent organic frameworks.

title: Water at the molecular frontier
abstract: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinement and interfacial forces produce a range of behaviours absent in the bulk. Sometimes this amounts to a renormalization of bulk properties; in other cases, new and non-intuitive phenomena emerge - exotic phases, anomalous transport, and dielectric responses that defy continuum expectations. reason: Perspective on nanoscale water behavior in confinement, relevant to desalination and filtration technologies.

abstract: Electrokinetic actuation enables non-contact fluid transport and particle manipulation in microfluidic devices. Induced-charge electrokinetics (ICEK) is particularly attractive for AC-field actuation because it can generate strong electrohydrodynamic motion without fixed surface charges. title: A Semi-Analytical Quantum-Cooperative Model of Proton Transport in Narrow Single-File Channels
abstract: Quantum behavior of protons in their transport through narrow, single-file water channels is an increasingly hot topic of discussion due to its possible far-reaching effects on fundamental biological and bioenergetic activities. It is well understood that ions move in an environment where there is electro-diffusion due to the electric field and concentration gradients which classical electro-diffusion models can explain. However, such models fall short of a full explanation of proton transport especially when quantum tunneling plays a role. abstract: Buffer chemistry modulates colloidal impedance critically for label-free biosensing and electrokinetic diagnostics, yet classical models neglect buffer-specific interactions. abstract: A theoretical analysis is presented for the sedimentation potential of a dilute suspension of charged spherical colloidal particles in an uncharged polymer gel medium saturated with an electrolyte solution. abstract: Photoactive polymers hold promise for powering micromotors by converting light into energy. However, traditional energy polymers cannot catalyze on one side of Janus structures in chemically driven micromotors because they only store and convert energy, not perform efficient photocatalysis. abstract: Single-reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co-amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. abstract: The present work develops an analytical model for electroosmotic peristaltic transport of a Williamson fluid in a flexible annular channel. title: Splitting probabilities for Brownian motion with diffusing boundaries: Application to polymer translocation
abstract: We study the translocation of a polymer chain through a nanopore where the chain length fluctuates stochastically due to the polymerization-depolymerization processes at the chain ends. title: Dynamic clustering of active chemotactic Janus particles
abstract: Modeling self-propulsion as an emergent diffusiophoretic effect, we come back to the dynamic clustering experiment of active Janus colloids. Working in the original three-dimensional geometry, and using the chemical solute concentration as a control parameter, we find that the dynamic clustering region occupies a robust fraction of the phase diagram. This behavior is rationalized using a linear stability analysis that efficiently captures the instability of the gas phase to dynamic clusters. abstract: Reverse electrodialysis (RED) is an emerging process intensification technology for sustainable energy generation from the salinity gradient between concentrated brines and dilute streams. abstract: Electroosmotic magnetohydrodynamic (EMHD) nanofluid transport in porous microchannels is important for controlling fluid flow and heat transfer in microscale thermal-management and microfluidic systems. This study investigates the effects of suction/injection and induced magnetic field on EMHD mixed-convection flow of Cu/water, SnO₂/water, and SiO₂/water nanofluids in a porous vertical microchannel. The flow is assumed to be steady, laminar, incompressible, Newtonian, and electrically conducting, with electroosmotic forcing, applied and induced magnetic fields, mixed convection, porous resistance, velocity and thermal slip, streaming potential, viscous dissipation, and wall mass transfer incorporated into the model. title: Statistical Optimization of Electrocoagulation on Membrane Fouling During Electrodialysis Process of Run‐Off Water Loaded With Road De‐Icing Salts
abstract: ABSTRACT To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study to investigate how the lifespan and performance of ion‐exchange membranes are affected during electrodialysis of run‐off water laden with road de‐icing salts. This study focuses on optimizing electrocoagulation (EC) and sand filtration as pretreatment methods to reduce membrane clogging in electrodialysis desalination of road run‐off water from de‐icing salts (RRWs). The goal was to minimize membrane fouling. Using factorial and central composite designs, 26 experiments were conducted to identify optimal EC conditions for turbidity and suspended solids (SS) removal. Results showed that electrolysis time was the most significant factor, achieving 78% SS and 86% turbidity removal. title: Analytical investigation of dual streaming potentials in electroosmotic magnetohydrodynamic nanofluid flow with induced magnetic field
abstract: This study presents an analytical investigation of electroosmotic magnetohydrodynamic (EMHD) mixed convection nanofluid flow in a vertical microchannel with induced magnetic field, Joule heating, viscous dissipation, and electrokinetic effects. Salt water is employed as the base fluid, while copper (Cu), tin oxide (SnO₂), and silicon dioxide (SiO₂) nanoparticles are comparatively investigated. The coupled nonlinear governing equations are transformed into dimensionless form and solved analytically using the Homotopy Perturbation Method (HPM). A distinguishing feature of the formulation is the nonlinear dual streaming-potential model generated by the Joule-heating term, from which the physically admissible streaming-potential branch is identified through convergence and limiting-case validation. abstract: This review treats selective ion separation in polymeric membrane systems as a design problem rather than as a fixed material property. To address the gap between laboratory performance and process-level relevance, a three-dimensional analytical framework that integrates transport mechanism, dynamic structural state, and separation-matrix complexity is proposed. Five research streams are compared: polymer inclusion membranes, ion-exchange membranes and electrodialysis, nanostructured and subnanometric frameworks, composite architectures, and polymer inclusion membrane - electrodialysis (PIM-ED) hybrids. abstract: This study develops an analytical model for peristaltic-electroosmotic transport of an ionic Jeffrey fluid in a magnetised ciliated microchannel. title: Self-adhering conductive hydrogel–wood scaffold for multidirectional wearable sensors
abstract: Conductive hydrogels are promising for wearable sensors, but the accurate resolution of human motions is limited by their isotropic network structures, while an intrinsic trade-off also exists between interfacial adhesion and mechanical robustness. Here, a wood-guided asymmetric bilayer conductive hydrogel is developed to integrate anisotropic sensing, mechanical support, and intrinsic skin adhesion within a single material system. The asymmetric architecture integrates a wood-reinforced polyvinyl alcohol/phytic acid (PVA/PA) top layer for anisotropic mechanical support with a PA-enriched bottom layer that enables compliant and robust skin adhesion, achieved through freeze-thaw-induced interfacial crystallite entanglement. title: Automated nanopore sensing by current-feedback membrane reformation
abstract: Stochastic nanopore sensing relies on large numbers of current blockage signals for statistical molecular analysis. Automated formation of planar bilayer lipid membranes (pBLMs) has been reported, but sustaining a single biological nanopore remains challenging, since nanopore reconstitution is inherently probabilistic. Here, we report an automated, current-feedback nanopore sensing platform that autonomously sustains single alpha-hemolysin (αHL) nanopores through repeated pBLM reformation. The sensing platform locates the pBLM formation position by measuring membrane capacitance, recognizes nanopore reconstitution through ion current feedback, and automatically reforms the pBLM once multiple nanopores have reconstituted. title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Solution Transport Properties in CSH/SiO2 Nanochannels Under High-Temperature and Water-Rich Environments
abstract: This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to construct a CSH/SiO2 nanochannel model, systematically investigating the dynamic transport behavior of pure water and Na2SO4 solution within the pores across temperatures ranging from 293 K to 368 K. title: Hierarchical anisotropic hydrogel with aligned ion-conducting channels for non-invasive brain–computer interface electrodes
abstract: Abstract Flexible hydrogel electrodes represent promising candidates for brain–computer interfaces (BCIs), however, achieving simultaneous high conductivity, mechanical compliance, and long-term durability remains a challenge. Herein, we report a conductive hydrogel with hierarchical anisotropic structures fabricated through an in situ directionally frozen copolymerization approach. This approach generates a dual-scale architecture featuring aligned vertical microchannels for ion transport and interconnected nanoporous networks for enhanced electronic conduction. Such a hierarchical design contributes to favorable electrical properties, offering an improvement in conductivity over conventional hydrogel electrodes. title: Membrane‐Assisted Capacitive Deionization by Electrically Conductive Composite Electrodes Enforced With PANI: Process Optimization and Scale up
abstract: ABSTRACT Innovative nanostructured composite electrodes were developed by integrating a PVA‐based ion‐exchange membrane onto a modified graphite substrate coated with a porous PVDF/activated carbon (AC) layer reinforced with polyaniline (PANI). This architecture enhances both ion selectivity and electrical conductivity, thus mitigating key capacitive deionization (CDI) limitations, such as inefficient ion separation, high internal resistance, and restricted electrochemical utilization of adsorption sites. The electrochemical behavior of the electrodes was characterized using cyclic voltammetry (CV), while desalination performance was evaluated in a membrane capacitive deionization (MCDI) system. title: Chlor-alkali electrolysis for battery grade lithium hydroxide production as a pathway towards low-carbon lithium refining
abstract: Lithium hydroxide (LiOH) is a critical precursor for nickel rich lithium-ion battery cathodes, with demand projected to grow rapidly over the next decade. Conventional LiOH production relies on multi-step chemical refining, which is energy intensive, reagent intensive and generates substantial byproduct streams. In this work, we evaluate LiCl based chlor-alkali electrolysis as a process intensified route for LiOH production and compare it with chemical routes and other electrochemical routes including bipolar membrane electrodialysis and electro-electrodialysis across energy use, CO 2 footprint and chemical waste generation. abstract: Lipoproteins, macromolecular assemblies of lipids and apolipoproteins, play a central role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Patients with healthy LDL-C levels can still develop ASCVD because the same amount of cholesterol can be contained in fewer large particles or many smaller ones. These smaller particles can circulate more easily in arteries and are more prone to penetrate the arterial lining, resulting in deposition and oxidation. abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are emerging as a programmable platform for solid electrolytes in solid‐state lithium batteries, since their crystalline, periodically ordered nanochannels can be engineered to enable directional ion transport. These low‐resistance pathways promote directional lithium‐ion (Li + ) migration through a narrower, more spatially ordered distribution of coordination environments, achieved via site‐to‐site hopping and/or guest‐assisted vehicular motion within the channels. This review presents a design‐oriented framework linking COF structural descriptors to ion‐transport metrics through a cause‐effect‐performance relationship. title: Performance and stability of commercial anion exchange membranes for hydrogen peroxide production in a dual-membrane electrolyser
abstract: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs) are a key component in the dual-membrane electrolyser for the electrochemical production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). However, their limited performance and chemical stability remain a major limitation for the practical implementation of this process. In this work, seven commercially available AEMs were systematically evaluated with respect to their properties, chemical stability, ex situ performance and in situ performance in a dual-membrane electrolyser. The results show that electrolyser performance is strongly influenced by membrane water management, with dehydration occurring at higher current densities. abstract: Abstract Single-molecule protein sequencing promises to democratize clinical proteomics, but platforms retrofitting static DNA-sequencing nanopores face a fundamental biophysical bottleneck: they only measure one-dimensional excluded volume. title: Stability and reliability of carbon-coated solid-state nanopores for single molecule analysis
abstract: Solid-state nanopores has shown great potential for analyzing single molecules. Electron beam-induced carbon deposition enables precise tuning of nanopore dimension to adapt different molecule sizes. In this work, we investigate the stability of carbon-coated Si and SiN nanopores in a nanopore-gated nanocavity device, during electrical measurements in various solutions. Our results show that the conductance of bare nanopores increase over the measurement time, indicating pore expansion caused by electrochemical corrosion of the nanopore walls. title: Micromanipulation With Dielectrophoretic Forces: A Review
abstract: This review article critically assesses dielectrophoretic (DEP) micromanipulation and methodically examines the discrepancies between theoretical predictions and practical results in cell sorting, trapping, and biological applications. title: Controlled Substrate Crossover from Cathode to Anode for Long-Term Autonomous Operation of Microbial Fuel Cells: A Transport–Reaction Modeling Study
abstract: Abstract Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) have been widely investigated as decentralized bioelectrochemical systems capable of converting organic substrates into electricity. However, their long-term autonomous operation is constrained by substrate depletion in the anode compartment, leading to metabolic starvation of electroactive biofilms and a decline in power output. title: Multi-objective optimisation of renewable energy integration in circular brine valorisation/treatment: The case of the CARMEn chain
abstract: Circular brine-valorisation chains offer a promising route to address water scarcity and critical raw-material recovery, but their large electrical and thermal energy demands can offset environmental benefits if powered by fossil sources. title: Coupling electric and magnetic dipoles in Janus nanoplatelets via surface-selective hybridization
abstract: Coupling electric and magnetic dipoles within nanoscale building blocks offers a promising strategy for creating hybrid materials with coupled magnetic and electric functionality. Here, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept approach for realizing this concept in Janus nanoparticles through surface-selective hybridization of ferrimagnetic barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets, selectively hybridized on one basal plane with organic polar ligands bearing a large electric dipole and a phosphonic anchoring group. The resulting Janus magneto-electric nanohybrids exhibit magnetic and electric dipoles oriented normal to the nanoplatelet basal plane. title: AC Electrokinetics-Enhanced Capacitive Aptasensor for Point-of-Care Testing of Acrylamide in Coffee
abstract: Acrylamide (AA) is a common contaminant in foods processed at high temperatures and has attracted significant attention due to its potential neurotoxicity and carcinogenicity. Therefore, the development of a highly sensitive, highly selective sensing technology suitable for on-site detection is of great importance for ensuring food safety. In this study, an aptamer (Apt)-based capacitive AA sensor was developed based on the alternating current electrokinetics (ACEK) effect. The sensor utilizes an aptamer as the biomimetic recognition element, which can specifically recognize AA, thereby enabling quantitative detection. title: Impedance response of electrolytic cells with non-Debye relaxation time distributions at adsorbing electrodes
abstract: The dynamics or the statistical behavior of an adsorbing-desorbing surface is complex or even is hardly described by microscopic models. title: AI-assisted optoelectrokinetic control of active self-propelling micromotors for independent navigation with multimode motions
abstract: Agile and controllable motion is essential for active micromotors to navigate various microscale scenarios and manipulate the microscopic world, where parallel navigation and independent control are highly desirable. However, most micromotor navigation strategies suffer from limited agility and poor predictability, with motion typically confined to single-micromotor self-propulsion along predetermined trajectories. title: Improved diagnostic identification of urothelial carcinoma through solid-state nanopore determination of urinary hyaluronan size distribution
abstract: Abstract Urothelial carcinoma (UC) is among the most common malignancies worldwide and is known to exhibit a high recurrence rate. The relative lack of validated, non-invasive biomarkers for the disease challenges early detection and negatively impacts patient outcomes. The linear polysaccharide hyaluronan (HA) has been recognized as a potential source of diagnostic information for UC, with its urinary concentration shown to be predictive of disease severity. Here, we use solid-state nanopore (SSNP) sensing to investigate the value of urinary HA size distribution as an independent and complementary predictor of UC. title: Nanopore‐Based Multiparametric Single‐Molecule Protein Detection: From Structural Analysis to Clinical Translation
abstract: Single-molecule protein analysis is crucial for elucidating biological processes and enabling early disease diagnosis. Nanopore sensing technology, owing to its label-free operation, high throughput, and direct electrical readout, has emerged as a highly promising platform for protein analysis. This review summarizes recent advances in nanopore-based protein analysis, with an emphasis on the detection of both folded and unfolded proteins.
